title: Sport Education as a Catalyst for Mental Health: a Predictive Model of Sports Enjoyment and Digital Challenges in China and South Asia — ES: La educación deportiva como catalizador para la salud mental: un modelo predictivo de disfrute deportivo y desafíos digitales en China y Asia meridional
authors: Ren, Guangtao; Abu Saad, Hazizi; Yaacob, Azhar; Yuan, Chuang; Liu, Meng
summary: This study investigates the complex relationships among sport education, digital behaviors, and mental health in university students from China and South Asia. We developed an integrated conceptual framework grounded in Self-Determination Theory (SDT) to examine how sports enjoyment and social media addiction jointly mediate the relationship between structured sport education and psychological outcomes. We collected primary data using a cross-sectional design from a balanced multinational sample of N=612 university students (308 from China and 304 from South Asia). We evaluated the data using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in two stages: measurement and structural models. The results indicate lower psychological distress, though both the structural components of sport education and the intrinsic level of sports enjoyment predict this outcome differently. Sports enjoyment (β = -0.310) is a stronger predictor of reduced social media addiction than the structural components of sport education (β = -0.190). Social media addiction is an important competing factor, as it can partly reduce the mental health benefits of taking part in sports. The PLSpredict analysis shows strong predictive power, especially for psychological distress (Q2 predict up to 0.428). These findings suggest that sport education primarily helps by playing sports more enjoyable and reducing digital addiction. The study points out that educators should focus on making sports enjoyable to support mental health and digital well-being, especially in demanding academic settings where digital use is high.

summary_es: Este estudio investiga las complejas relaciones entre educación deportiva, comportamientos digitales y salud mental en estudiantes universitarios de China y Asia meridional. Desarrollamos un marco conceptual integrado basado en la teoría de autodeterminación (SDT) para examinar cómo el disfrute deportivo y la adicción a las redes sociales median conjuntamente la relación entre la educación deportiva estructurada y los resultados psicológicos. Recopilamos datos primarios utilizando un diseño transversal de una muestra multinacional equilibrada de estudiantes universitarios N=612 (308 de China y 304 de Asia meridional). Evaluamos los datos usando el Modelado de Ecuación Estructural (PLS-SEM) en dos etapas: modelos de medición y estructurales. Los resultados indican una menor angustia psicológica, aunque tanto los componentes estructurales de la educación deportiva como el nivel intrínseco del disfrute deportivo predicen este resultado de manera diferente. El disfrute deportivo (β = -0.310) es un predictor más fuerte de la reducción de la adicción a las redes sociales que los componentes estructurales de la educación deportiva (β = -0.190). La adicción a los medios sociales es un factor competidor importante, ya que en parte puede reducir los beneficios de la salud mental de participar en los deportes. El análisis PLSpredict muestra un fuerte poder predictivo, especialmente para la angustia psicológica (Q2 predice hasta 0,428). Estos resultados sugieren que la educación deportiva ayuda principalmente jugando deportes más agradables y reduciendo la adicción digital. El estudio señala que los educadores deben centrarse en hacer deportes agradables para apoyar la salud mental y el bienestar digital, especialmente en entornos académicos exigentes donde el uso digital es alto.

title: Integrating Service-Learning to Promote Inclusion in Teacher Training — ES: Integrar el aprendizaje de servicios para promover la inclusión en la formación de maestros
authors: López García-Torres, Rocío; Saneleuterio, Elia; Andreu Ato, Nuria
summary: This article presents and analyzes a service-learning (SL) project funded by a private Spanish university during eight years and implemented in its Childhood and Primary Education degree programs to foster inclusive training methods. The pedagogical design follows a thorough review of the theoretical framework underlying its practical and educative significance. The project integrates the preparation of both qualified educators and socially committed citizens, promoting a shift in educational paradigms to meet the demands of an evolving social reality. Grounded in the SL methodology, the initiative seeks concrete ways to involve students in activities of institutions serving individuals with disabilities, focusing on the field of special educational needs. The analysis of this SL project demonstrates multiple benefits for both future teachers and partner organizations. From the perspective of service delivery, the participating associations report that students effectively addressed their needs and expectations. From the students’ perspective, SL fosters not only curricular learning but also significant personal growth (social impact, empathy, ethic of care…). The insights and competencies acquired through this experience are essential for individuals who will enter the educational system as professionals and have to address diversity in their classrooms and effectively promote the inclusion of their future disadvantaged student

title: ¿Es la educación emprendedora más importante que la resiliencia? un análisis de moderación de la intención emprendedora en jóvenes del Perú
authors: Rojas Nina, Jorge Eloy; Cutipa Rodriguez, Jimmy; Medina Gamez, Kristhian Pattrik; Cuba Pacheco, Luz Gabriela; Velazco Gonzales, Alfredo; Laura Pumaleque, Lismer Yamil; Cuti Saico, Dino Franco; Flores Chávez, Susan Marlen
summary: The aim of this study was to analyze the mediating and moderating roles of entrepreneurial education (EE) in the relationship between entrepreneurial resilience (ER) and entrepreneurial intention (EI). A quantitative, non-experimental methodology was employed. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) was used for data analysis. The sample consisted of 379 undergraduate business students from a public university in southern Peru, selected through non-probabilistic convenience sampling. Data were collected via a self-administered questionnaire using Likert-type scales. The results confirm that resilience has a positive impact on entrepreneurial intention (EI) and entrepreneurial education (EE), suggesting that resilient students maximize the entrepreneurial learning they obtain. EE has a direct positive effect on EI and partially mediates the influence of psychological resources. Additionally, a negative moderating effect of education was found on the relationship between resilience and intention (β=−0.101). The overall model explains 53.6% of the variance in entrepreneurial intention. Resilience and education are important predictors of entrepreneurship. When university education is high, entrepreneurial intention relies less on resilience because the university provides techniques and networks that substitute for resilience. It is recommended to integrate technical training with the development of resilience competencies into university curricula

title: A Quantitative Study on the Participation, Influencing Factors, and Perceived Efficacy of International Exchange among Fujian Undergraduates under the Background of the Maritime Silk Road — ES: Estudio cuantitativo sobre la participación, los factores de influencia y la eficacia percibida del intercambio internacional entre los pregrados de Fujian bajo el fondo de la carretera marítima de seda
summary: International exchange is a flagship instrument of higher-education internationalization, yet participation is often socially patterned and the educational value students perceive is shaped by institutional implementation. This study investigates the participation rate, influencing factors, and perceived efficacy of international exchange among Fujian undergraduates within a Maritime Silk Road–oriented internationalization environment. Using a 2025 multi-institution survey of 1,200 undergraduates from eight Fujian higher-education institutions, the study models realized exchange participation with logistic regression including institution fixed effects and estimates perceived efficacy using covariate-adjusted linear models. To address observable selection into participation, inverse probability weighting is applied with balance diagnostics and sensitivity checks for extreme weights. Results show that realized participation is 17.5% and is most strongly associated with opportunity conditions, particularly awareness and perceived institutional support, alongside socioeconomic resources, language proficiency, and exchange-related aid. Risk/safety concerns are negatively associated with completion. Participation is positively associated with higher perceived efficacy across intercultural, academic, career, and adaptability domains; the adjusted association remains substantively meaningful and persists under selection-aware robustness. Heterogeneity analyses indicate stronger participation-linked efficacy among lower-SES students and in environments with higher institutional support. The findings highlight that equitable internationalization depends not only on expanding opportunities but also on reducing information frictions, strengthening advising and administrative coherence, and designing affordability support that addresses indirect and upfront costs so that mobility pathways translate into inclusive educational value.

summary_es: El intercambio internacional es un instrumento insignia de la internacionalización de la educación superior, pero la participación a menudo se caracteriza socialmente y el valor educativo que perciben los estudiantes está conformado por la implementación institucional. Este estudio investiga el tipo de participación, los factores de influencia y la eficacia percibida del intercambio internacional entre los pregrados Fujian dentro de un entorno de internacionalización orientado a la Ruta Marítima de la Seda. Mediante una encuesta multiinstitucional de 2025 de 1.200 graduados de ocho instituciones de educación superior de Fujian, los modelos de estudio realizaron la participación en el intercambio con regresión logística, incluidos los efectos fijos institucionales y las estimaciones percibidas de eficacia utilizando modelos lineales ajustados por covariada. Para abordar la selección observable en participación, el ponderado de probabilidad inversa se aplica con diagnóstico de equilibrio y controles de sensibilidad para pesos extremos. Los resultados muestran que la participación efectiva es del 17,5% y está más fuertemente asociada con las condiciones de oportunidad, en particular la conciencia y el apoyo institucional percibido, junto con los recursos socioeconómicos, la competencia lingüística y la ayuda relacionada con el intercambio. Los problemas de riesgo/seguridad están asociados negativamente a la terminación. La participación se asocia positivamente con una mayor eficacia percibida en los ámbitos interculturales, académicos, de carrera y adaptabilidad; la asociación ajustada sigue siendo sustancialmente significativa y persiste bajo la robustez consciente de la selección. Los análisis de heterogeneidad indican una mayor eficacia vinculada a la participación entre los estudiantes de menor nivel y en entornos con mayor apoyo institucional. Las conclusiones ponen de relieve que la internacionalización equitativa depende no sólo de la ampliación de las oportunidades sino también de la reducción de las fricciones de información, el fortalecimiento de la asesoría y la coherencia administrativa, y el diseño de apoyo a la asequibilidad que aborde los costos indirectos y iniciales para que las vías de movilidad se traduzcan en un valor educativo inclusivo.

title: The Managed Academic: performance Metrics and Identity Transformation among Faculty in Massified Higher Education
summary: The expansion of higher education has intensified the use of performance measurement that effectively altered the role and identity of the faculty. Reliance on quantifiable factors such as research output, student ratings, and teaching success has been criticized in terms of its influence on the autonomy of the faculty and the profession. Though such changes can prove important to comprehend, there is a gap in the research in comprehending how such metrics can influence faculty at the individual level. This gap is what this research aims to address by exploring what impact that performance indicators have on faculty identity and autonomy in massified higher education systems. Peer-reviewed articles published during the period between 2015 and 2026 were analyzed using the systematic literature review (SLR) methodology. The significant findings are that the performance measures, despite being supposed to promote accountability and improve the performance of an institution, are may lead to the process of narrowing the faculty roles and the shift in professional identity. Professional staff is being pressurized to incorporate their educational activities into the institutional goals at the cost of their autonomy. The implications of these findings suggest that the performance measures, as important as they are to institutional judgment, need to be reconsidered to become less strict, and supportive of the complexity of faculty performance to foster a moderate approach to faculty freedom and institutional requirements.

title: AI, Education, and International Student Engagement in Chinese Universities: implications for Policy and Learning Equity
authors: Sun, Jingyi; Bin Sulaiman, Tajularipin; Binti Razali, Fazilah
summary: This study investigates the roles of Anxiety, Teacher Support, and Academic Self-Efficacy in shaping foreign university students’ engagement in Chinese language learning. Specifically, it examines the mediating role of AI-Acceptance in this dynamic. Drawing on Social Cognitive Theory (SCT) and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), a quantitative survey was conducted with 528 foreign students across eight universities in Liaoning Province, China. title: Conceptualización y mediación docente del enfoque Amazonía como sujeto de derechos en una escuela rural amazónica

title: Toward Deployable Examination Paper Generation for Cross-Major Programming Assessment: a PRISMA-Guided Review of Multi-Constraint Optimisation and Hybrid GA-SA
authors: Lin, Xu; Othman, Marini; Ting, Tin Tin; Wang, Yuhang
summary: Automated Examination Paper Generation (EPG) has become a critical component of programming education, particularly in contexts where a common item bank is required to support multiple student cohorts characterised by varying difficulty levels, cognitive priorities, and skill-coverage needs. To establish a review-informed foundation for the practical design of deployable EPG systems in such environments, this study undertakes a PRISMA 2020-guided systematic literature review that conceptualises EPG as a multi-constraint combinatorial optimisation problem. By adopting a conservative evidence boundary together with a two-tier coding framework, the review integrates the ways in which earlier studies have operationalised structural requirements, difficulty levels, score allocation, skill coverage, Bloom’s taxonomy-aligned cognitive domains, and efficiency-related performance measures. In parallel, it critically examines whether these studies provide deployment-relevant details, including item-bank metadata, transparency in constraint-handling procedures, trade-off decision rules, benchmark comparisons, and evidence relating to runtime performance and scalability. Across the reviewed literature, solution approaches extend from basic heuristics and exact optimisation models to metaheuristic methods, hybrid GA-SA architectures, and learning-augmented techniques. The synthesis indicates that hybrid GA-SA is consistently presented as a credible engineering framework for addressing dense, multi-objective EPG problems. Nevertheless, the existing body of literature remains limited by incomplete methodological reporting, insufficient machine-readable formalisation of pedagogical objectives, and a lack of evidence relevant to governance and implementation. Rather than asserting the universal superiority of any single algorithm, this review converts diverse findings into a deployability-oriented synthesis grounded in MCDM principles. Four major design implications are identified for programming-focused EPG systems: clearly defined and auditable constraints, Bloom- and skill-aligned parameter specification, teacher-in-the-loop calibration mechanisms, and reproducible evaluation procedures. Collectively, these findings establish a defensible link between algorithmic selection and pedagogical application, while also providing a robust evidence base for future hybrid GA-SA development in cross-major programming assessment contexts.

title: The Construction of a Mezzo-Soprano Pedagogical Framework from a Cultural Adaptation Perspective-A Grounded Theory Analysis Based on the Experiences of Mezzo-Soprano Educators and Students from China and the West
summary: Against the backdrop of deepening global integration in music education, how to scientifically introduce and effectively integrate Western bel canto mezzo-soprano pedagogy into China’s indigenous vocal system has become a significant academic concern. Differences between Western training and Chinese vocal traditions—in vocal techniques, aesthetic orientations, and pedagogical philosophies—generate challenges in localization, aesthetic conflict, and the balance between national identity and international standards. Existing studies often rely on technical transplantation or experiential discussion, lacking solid theoretical grounding and systematic empirical evidence. This study therefore adopts acculturation theory as its core lens to reveal the mechanisms underlying Sino-Western integration in mezzo-soprano teaching. It aims to construct a scientific cross-cultural pedagogical framework, offer theoretical and practical guidance for mezzo-soprano training in China, and provide an empirical case that challenges the long-standing assumption of “one-way technical borrowing.” The study applies acculturation theory as its theoretical foundation and employs grounded theory as its primary methodological approach to avoid bias caused by pre-established assumptions. The research involves eight participants: four vocal educators (two European and two Chinese) and four students with educational experience in both Chinese and Western conservatories. Data were collected through semi-structured in-depth interviews focusing on teaching philosophy, technical adaptation, aesthetic cognition, and cross-cultural learning experiences. Data analysis followed grounded theory’s three-stage coding procedure. Open coding generated initial concepts; axial coding established relationships among categories; and selective coding identified the core category and integrated it into a coherent theoretical model. This process ensures both systematic analysis and the rigor required for inductive theory building. The research yields a “cross-cultural mezzo-soprano teaching framework” comprising three interrelated dimensions. First, Technical Creative Transformation emphasizes that Western vocal techniques must undergo creative adaptation when applied in the Chinese context. Adjustments should consider Mandarin phonetic features, Chinese vocal aesthetics, and the demands of local repertoire rather than relying on mechanical transplantation. Second, Aesthetic Negotiation Dialogue captures the dynamic process through which Western and Chinese vocal aesthetics move from conflict to coexistence. authors: Yaemyuean, Anan; Sakdapat, Naksit; Nonthachot, Perawat; Pundontong, Nattapong
summary: The main objectives of this experimental research were 1) to develop and evaluate the effectiveness of a training program designed to modify psychological traits on environmental conservation, 2) to assess the achievement outcomes of the training program on attitudes in three dimensions, and 3) to analyze the long-term retention of attitudes and the scalability of the program across different areas. The study employed a Two-Group Pretest-Posttest-Follow-up Design. The sample consisted of 160 purposively selected youths aged 13–15 years from Uttaradit Province, equally divided into an experimental group and a control group (N=80). The research instruments included a training program developed based on Experiential Learning Theory and Positive Psychology, integrating proactive activities such as concept mapping for environmental problem analysis and role-playing activities to cultivate environmental ethics. The program was validated by a panel of experts, achieving a perfect Item-Objective Congruence (IOC) index of 1.00 for all items. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and inferential statistics, including Repeated Measures ANOVA and Least Significant Difference (LSD) multiple comparison tests. The major findings revealed that; 1) the training program designed to promote positive attitudes towards environmental conservation among Thai youth were effective based on the academic criteria. 2) After participating in the training program, youths in the experimental group demonstrated significantly higher mean scores in all three attitude dimensions including evaluative cognition, feelings, and behavioral intention towards environmental conservation, compared with the control group (p < 0.01). Post Hoc analysis indicated that post-training and follow-up scores were significantly higher than pre-training scores. Meanwhile, no significant difference was found between post-training and follow-up scores, suggesting the sustained effect of the training. 3) Repeated measures analysis based on ANOVA further confirmed that these differences were statistically significant (p < 0.01). The Post Hoc results also showed that both post-experimental and follow-up (2 months later) scores were significantly higher than pre-experimental scores. Without significant difference between post-experimental and follow-up periods, it reflected the persistence and stability of the psychological traits. 4) The implementation of the program in other areas yielded consistent results, confirming the resilience and effectiveness of the innovative approaches to changing youth attitudes broadly. This research proposes a new conceptual foundation for environmental education management by demonstrating that only cognitive dimensions and cognitive information transfer are insufficient to produce sustainable behavioral change. The key innovative concept of this study lies in the integration of affective dimensions and emotional engagement (Affective Integration) together with psychological readiness as mediating mechanisms that connect knowledge to internalized intention. This process transforms youth from passive learners into intrinsically motivated conservationists who possess an emotional commitment to nature. Such transformation constitutes a fundamental basis for the development of green citizenship characterized by responsibility towards the dynamic challenges of the 21st century. The findings further confirm that the intervention model employed in this study demonstrates empirical effectiveness in simultaneously enhancing knowledge, attitudes, and behavioral intentions in an integrated manner. Consequently, the model can serve as a principal framework for policies related to core curriculum development or the design of extracurricular activities in educational institutions that emphasize behavioral outcomes rather than merely knowledge-based assessment. Furthermore, the innovative training program functions as an operational prototype that local administrative organizations and civil society networks can adapt and scale up to create conservation-oriented learning processes in alignment with local cultural practices and ecological systems. This approach can strengthen community capacity for sustainable self-management of natural resources and reduce the gap between governmental policy and grassroots-level implementation.

title: The Mediating Role of Student Engagement in the Relationship between Personality Traits and Academic Innovation Performance — ES: Función mediadora de la participación estudiantil en la relación entre los hábitos de personalidad y el rendimiento académico de la innovación
authors: Sun, Qianru; Guo, Linzhi; Iglesias Tellado, María Luisa
summary: Due to the growing attention toward the academic innovation field and within the creative field of education, this paper will discuss the mediating power of student engagement on the ability of personality traits to shape the innovation performance of students. Based on the Five-Factor Model and the engagement theory, the study will seek to determine those traits that have a significant impact on innovation and the transfer of the personality into academic creativity in the form of engagement. The study employed a quantitative cross-sectional study design to sample 252 fourth-year undergraduate students taking undergraduate degree programs in drama, film, and television performance programs in five major Chinese universities. Self-report questions were validated and analyzed with the help of Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). It was found that openness, conscientiousness, and extraversion were great predictors of student engagement, which positively contributed to academic innovation performance. Innovation results were partially mediated by the effects that openness and conscientiousness had on the results of engagement. The results also point to engagement as an influential process between personality and innovation that can be used by teachers and policy-makers in an attempt to promote creative academic achievement. Incorporating personality-sensitive engagement principles into the curriculum design can contribute to innovation in the students. Future studies need to consider more longitudinal dynamics and investigate other mediators, including motivation, self-efficacy, or institutional support.

summary_es: Debido a la creciente atención hacia el campo de la innovación académica y dentro del campo creativo de la educación, este artículo discutirá el poder mediador del compromiso estudiantil sobre la capacidad de los rasgos de personalidad para dar forma al rendimiento de innovación de los estudiantes. Basado en el Modelo de Cinco-Factor y la teoría de compromiso, el estudio tratará de determinar los rasgos que tienen un impacto significativo en la innovación y la transferencia de la personalidad a la creatividad académica en forma de compromiso. El estudio empleó un diseño cuantitativo de estudios transversales para probar 252 estudiantes de grado cuarto que tomaron programas de grado en programas de teatro, cine y televisión en cinco grandes universidades chinas. Se validaron y analizaron las preguntas de auto-reportación con la ayuda de la Modelización de la Ecuación Estructural (PLS-SEM). Se encontró que la apertura, la conciencia y la extraversión eran grandes predictores de compromiso estudiantil, lo que contribuyó positivamente al rendimiento académico de innovación. Los resultados de la innovación fueron parcialmente mediados por los efectos que la apertura y la conciencia tenían sobre los resultados del compromiso. Los resultados también apuntan al compromiso como un proceso influyente entre la personalidad y la innovación que pueden ser utilizados por maestros y responsables de la formulación de políticas en un intento de promover el logro académico creativo. La incorporación de principios de compromiso sensibles a la personalidad en el diseño del plan de estudios puede contribuir a la innovación en los estudiantes. Los estudios futuros deben considerar más dinámicas longitudinales e investigar a otros mediadores, incluyendo motivación, autoeficacia o apoyo institucional.

title: Reconstructing Dance Education in the Digital Era: integrating Artificial Intelligence and Motion Capture for Innovative Talent Development — ES: Reconstructing Dance Education in the Digital Era: integrating Artificial Intelligence and Motion Capture for Innovative Talent Development
summary: It is in the nature of the digital transformation of dance education as a fundamental reconstructive imperative and not superficial use of technology. The systematic review considers the way in which artificial intelligence and motion capture technologies are transforming the talent development in performing arts education by evaluating 13 peer-reviewed studies. Based on the case studies of China, India, Singapore, Europe, and North America, such as the DSTEVF system, ReAL-T platform, Smart Steps framework, WhoDo project, and Moveally AI platform, this paper explores technical architectures, education results, and policy frameworks to regulate the technology integration. Results show that AI-motion capture technologies influence positively dance performance and self-efficacy (moderate to substantial effects), but provoke serious issues of preservation of embodied knowledge, transformation of professional identity of the teacher and equity of access. The analysis has a value to educational theory by re-conceptualizing the body-technology relation of postdigital pedagogy, and also provides comparative policy information to institutions that must make their way through this change.

title: Development of Transdisciplinary Integration Innovation to Promote Geo-literacy of High School Students
summary: The objectives of this research were threefold: 1) to investigate the historical development, systemic challenges, and structural limitations of the geography curriculum in Thailand; 2) to design and develop a transdisciplinary learning innovation aimed at promoting the geo-literacy of high school students; and 3) to evaluate the pedagogical effects of implementing this transdisciplinary innovation. Employing a sequential mixed-methods research design, the study gathered data from two distinct target groups: a panel of five subject-matter experts who evaluated the structural validity of the innovation, and an experimental group of 150 upper-secondary students who participated in the instructional intervention. The research instruments comprised a qualitative document synthesis protocol, an innovation suitability evaluation form, a comprehensive geo-literacy competency assessment, and a semi-structured focus group discussion matrix. Qualitative data underwent thematic content analysis, while quantitative metrics were analyzed using descriptive statistics ( S.D.) and inferential statistics (paired-samples t-test). The findings revealed that: 1) The evolution of the Thai geography curriculum progressed through four historical paradigms, shifting from spatial positivism aimed at territorial unification to a post-humanist framework within the contemporary Basic Education Core Curriculum. A critical systemic limitation identified was the persistent overemphasis on passive rote memorization and disjointed disciplinary silos, which broadens the gap between theoretical geography and real-world environmental phenomena. 2) The development of the Transdisciplinary Learning Innovation—operationalized through the Phenomenon-Based Transdisciplinary Boundary-Crossing (PB-TBC) mechanism and the Contour Model—synthesized geography into five core dimensions: Geo-Knowledge, Geo-Process, Geo-Abilities, Geo-Integration, and Geo-Literacy. Expert validation rated the overall quality of this instructional innovation at the highest qualitative level (=4.60, S.D.=0.67). 3) Empirical implementation demonstrated that the innovation significantly enhanced student competencies, with the post-test geo-literacy scores reaching an outstanding level ( =3.82, S.D.=0.40). Furthermore, inferential verification confirmed a statistically significant improvement in students’ spatial decision-making and problem-solving capacities (p<.05), proving that the innovation successfully transformed passive learners into proactive data creators capable of navigating complex socio-environmental challenges

title: A Study on the Influence Mechanism of Rural English Teachers’ AI Teaching Self-Efficacy from the Perspective of TPACK Theory
authors: Ling, Ziying; Wen, Anqi; Li, Xinyun; Huang, Yujian; Mo, Yongyi
summary: Based on the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) theoretical framework, this study employs a mixed-methods approach—combining questionnaire surveys and semi-structured interviews—to systematically investigate the current development status and internal influence mechanisms of TPACK capabilities and Artificial Intelligence (AI) teaching self-efficacy among 115 rural primary and secondary school English teachers in western Guangdong. The findings indicate that the overall TPACK capabilities and AI teaching self-efficacy of rural English teachers are at an upper-middle level. Across the TPACK dimensions, teachers exhibit an uneven developmental profile characterized by relatively solid foundational theoretical knowledge but weak higher-order capabilities in the deep integration of technology and subject disciplines. Regarding AI teaching self-efficacy, their mastery of basic AI knowledge significantly surpasses their confidence in higher-order practical applications such as teaching assessment. Furthermore, linear regression analysis confirms that TPACK capability has a significant positive predictive effect on AI teaching self-efficacy, explaining 41.2% of its variance. This study not only provides empirical evidence for enhancing rural English teachers' AI teaching integration capabilities and overcoming technology application bottlenecks, but also offers vital practical references for promoting the equitable digital development of rural education and innovating teacher training models.

title: Discretion Under Resource Constraints: school Administrators and China’s Silver Age Teaching Program
authors: Niu, Yaxin; Ajrun Khalid, Nur; Gao, Zhen
summary: Population aging and the uneven distribution of public service capacity are accelerating countries’ efforts to encourage retirees to participate in public services. China’s “Silver Age Teaching Program” recruits retired teachers to work in rural schools with scarce educational resources, thereby improving basic education provision in under-resourced areas. This study takes Bobai County in Guangxi—the county with the largest number of teachers recruited under the program—as the research site. Drawing on street-level bureaucracy (SLB) theory and employing a qualitative case study design involving field observation and semi-structured interviews, we analyse how school administrators’ discretion reshapes implementation pathways and policy outcomes. We find that, under conditions of persistently high student enrollment, chronic teacher shortages, and broadly defined policy texts, administrators prioritize practical solutions to immediate operational challenges through situational role allocation, selective task assignment, and experience-based judgment. These discretionary practices produce several outcomes, including the practical contraction of developmental objectives, the institutionalization of a gap-filling implementation mode, and the instrumentalization of silver-age teachers’ roles.

title: Pedagogical Innovation to Enhance Ethics Literacy of Pre-service Teachers within the Post Digital Citizenship Context
authors: Maidee, Wilaiwan; Mangkhang, Charin; Phuwanatwichit, Thongchai; Tayraukham, Sombat; Dibyamandala, Jarunee
summary: This research aimed to: (1) investigate the existing problems, needs, and theoretical foundations related to ethics literacy among pre-service teachers within the context of post-digital citizenship; (2) develop a pedagogical innovation to enhance ethics literacy; and (3) evaluate its effectiveness. The study employed a Research and Development (R&D) methodology consisting of four phases: investigating needs and theoretical foundations, developing the innovation, implementing the innovation, and evaluating its effectiveness. Participants included 266 individuals comprising key informants, experts, pre-service teachers, and stakeholders involved in teacher education. Data were collected through interviews, questionnaires, expert evaluations, ethics literacy assessments, and satisfaction surveys. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, while qualitative data were analyzed through content analysis. The findings revealed that pre-service teachers perceived a high need for ethics literacy development in response to the challenges of the post-digital era. The pedagogical innovation developed through the 5E Approach consisted of four instructional units: Exploring, Ethical Reasoning, Enacting Responsibility, and Embedding Findings. Expert evaluation indicated that the innovation demonstrated high levels of appropriateness, feasibility, and usefulness. Following implementation, participants showed a high level of ethics literacy across cognitive, affective, and behavioral dimensions. In addition, overall satisfaction with the innovation was at a high level. The study concludes that the proposed pedagogical innovation effectively enhances ethics literacy among pre-service teachers and provides a practical framework for integrating ethical learning into teacher education within post-digital citizenship contexts

title: The Impact of AI-Assisted Vocabulary Learning on EFL Students in Chinese Higher Vocational Colleges
authors: He, Chuanli; Binti Hashim, Harwati; Syafiqah Binti Yaccob, Nur
summary: This study examined the impact of AI-assisted vocabulary learning on EFL students in Chinese higher vocational colleges. The study focused on three independent variables: perceived usefulness of AI-assisted vocabulary learning, learning motivation and learning engagement. Vocabulary learning effectiveness was treated as the dependent variable. A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was adopted, and data were collected from 250 EFL students in Chinese higher vocational colleges in Sichuan Province, China. The questionnaire contained demographic items and Likert-scale items measuring the four main constructs. SPSS was used to conduct frequency analysis, reliability analysis, Pearson correlation and multiple regression analysis. The findings showed that AI tools were widely used by respondents, with 60.8% using them often or very often for English vocabulary learning. Reliability results confirmed excellent internal consistency for all scales. Correlation analysis showed strong positive relationships among perceived usefulness, learning motivation, learning engagement and vocabulary learning effectiveness. Regression results confirmed that all three predictors had significant positive effects on vocabulary learning effectiveness, with learning engagement emerging as the strongest predictor. The study concludes that AI-assisted vocabulary learning can enhance EFL vocabulary outcomes when students perceive AI tools as useful, remain motivated and actively engage in learning activities.

title: Comportamiento prosocialidad e identidad pedagógica en el profesorado en formación: dimensiones vocacionales, emocionales yrelacionales en la formación inicial docente
authors: Contreras Parraguez, Pilar Andrea; Castro, Ricardo; Sánchez Bravo, Alejandra Del Carmen; Belmar Mellado, Marta Ester; Jaramillo Azema, Cristian Alonso
summary: This research focused on caracterizing the pedagogical profile and the prosocial behavior of pre-service teachers at chilean universities. A quantitative, non experimental descriptive transverse design was chosen, using a sample of 825 pedagogy students from 4 majors: kindergarten education, elementary education, high school education and special education. Two instruments were applied: a semantic differencial to asses the pedagogical profile dimensions (education, learning, student and teacher) and a prosociality scale of 24 items structured in four dimensions (empathy, cooperation, prosocial leadership and respect). The results show high levels of empathy and cooperation, along with a sustained academic commitment and a reflective appraisal of the learning process. On the other hand, moderate values in leadership and normative coexistence were found. This shows a prosocial orientation centered on support and interpersonal sensibility more than on control or authority. Descriptive differences by gender and career show a bigger prosociality on kindergarten education and special education students. These findings confirm that prosociality behavior and socioemotional skills are structural components of the pedagogical profile and emergent teacher identity coherent with professional background and socioemotional learning. The study highlights the need to redefine teacher training programs by integrating modules on emotional education, reflexive tutorial and cooperative learning. Finally, it is proposed to advance towards to transcultural and longitudinal studies that analize the development of teacher identity and its decisive prosocial through analytic and integrated approaches, so contributing to design fomatives models more ethical, inclusive and sustainable.

title: Liderazgo educativo y el uso de inteligencia artificial en la educación pública de la UGEL Sur Arequipa
authors: Romero Carazas, Rafael; Bernedo Moreira, David Hugo; Valero Ancco, Vidnay Noel; Atahuasi Chaparro, Jesús; Espiritu Martinez, Antony Paul; Cahuapaza Morales, Augusto; Bazualdo Fiorini, Enzo Renatto; Delgado Talavera, James Jair
summary: Through the integration of educational leadership and artificial intelligence, education can experience a paradigm shift toward a more creative, personalized, and efficient system, all while maintaining a commitment to ethics and placing the needs of students at the center. The objective of the study is to determine the relationship between educational leadership and the use of artificial intelligence in public education of UGEL Sur Arequipa. The research methodology was quantitative, non-experimental, and used the structural equation modeling (SEM) method. A total of 352 teachers with managerial responsibilities were selected and surveyed. According to the results, 72.1% of the participants have a good perception of educational leadership, while 73.1% indicated that they support the use of AI in public education. Likewise, the proposed SEM model demonstrated that educational leadership and its dimensions are correlated with the use of artificial intelligence in education, obtaining significant value (0.901). It is concluded that educational leadership in UGEL Sur Arequipa is positively and significantly correlated with the use of AI in public education

title: Autoeficacia, bienestar y rendimiento académico como predictores de aspiraciones educativas en secundaria en Chile
summary: Educational aspirations during adolescence are influenced by multiple academic and psychosocial factors that shape students’ future educational trajectories. This study examined the relationship between self-efficacy, mental wellbeing, and academic performance in shaping the educational aspirations of high school students. Following concurrent mixed-methods, non-experimental, cross-sectional design, data from 126 students were analyzed through ordinal logistic regression, based on a questionnaire that included the General Self-Efficacy Scale and the Warwick-Edinburgh Mental Well-being Scale. The qualitative data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. The results indicate that students with higher grades and greater mental wellbeing tend to project higher educational goals, particularly regarding progression to higher education. In contrast, general self-efficacy did not show a significant relationship with these aspirations. The reflexive thematic analysis revealed that students’ educational aspirations toward higher education are shaped through tensions between motivations for personal growth, social mobility, and professional identity, and the academic, socioeconomic, and emotional barriers they perceive in their trajectories. Findings suggest that educational aspirations are constructed as multifactorial and emotionally situated processes, where wellbeing, self-concept, vocational uncertainty, and structural conditions converge in the projection of future educational pathways. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of considering both academic development and psychological wellbeing in the design of educational strategies aimed at strengthening students’ aspirations.

title: La derecha radical en Cataluña: Análisis comparativo de la ideología de Vox Cataluña y Aliança Catalana desde una perspectiva histórica
authors: Gómez Solano, Lorién; Seijo Boado, Ismael; Antón Mellón, Joan
summary: The aim of this paper is to provide a comparative analysis, from the intersection of political theory and history, of the ideology of the two main radical right-wing forces in Catalonia: Vox Catalonia and Aliança Catalana. After presenting the methodological foundations of the paper, the concept of the radical right is defined. Second, the cultural foundations and ideological references of Spanish and Catalan nationalism are examined comparatively. Next, the social causes and political antecedents of both movements—such as Plataforma per Catalunya and the xenophobic campaigns of the Partido Popular de Cataluña in Badalona—are analyzed. Finally, a qualitative content analysis is conducted of the electoral programs presented by both parties in the May 2024 elections to the Parliament of Catalonia, focusing on the following dimensions: national identity, immigration, security, and economic policy. The findings suggest that, despite constructing opposing forms of identity-based otherness, both Vox and Aliança Catalana can be classified as radical right-wing formations whose core ideas are rooted in similar foundations: an exclusionary, authoritarian ultranationalism grounded in the defense of the economic interests of the ruling classes.

title: Impacto de la elección de carreras STEM en el razonamiento cuantitativo: análisis diferencial por género y factores individuales y preuniversitarios
authors: Barrera Rodríguez, Ana María; Jaramillo Mejía, Víctor David; Echeverri Gutiérrez, Paola Andrea
summary: This study analyzes the impact of choosing STEM careers (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) on the development of quantitative reasoning and its differences by gender, pre-university factors, and individual characteristics. The research adopts a quantitative approach with an ex post facto design. Secondary data from the Saber 11 and Saber Pro assessments conducted by the Colombian Institute for the Evaluation of Education (ICFES) were used, complemented by primary data collected through surveys administered to 653 university students from Risaralda, Colombia. The analysis employed Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression models, Propensity Score Matching (PSM), and decision trees (CART) to estimate differential effects and explore patterns associated with the choice of STEM programs. The results indicate that enrolling in a STEM degree is associated with an average increase of approximately 7.6 points in quantitative reasoning competencies compared to non-STEM programs, an estimate that is consistent with a positive causal effect under the identification assumptions of PSM, but does not constitute definitive causal evidence given the observational nature of the data. Additionally, the quantitative reasoning gains associated with STEM careers are significantly smaller for women than for men, evidencing a gender gap in the educational returns of these disciplines. The decision tree segmentation analysis identified prior science performance, family educational capital, and area of residence as the factors with the greatest discriminant power in predicting the likelihood of women choosing STEM careers. The findings underscore the need to strengthen educational policies aimed at gender equity in STEM, with particular attention to building scientific competencies at the secondary education level and reducing territorial and socioeconomic disparities in access to STEM pathways.

title: ¿Confían los legisladores en sus Congresos? Un estudio comparado sobre sus determinantes individuales y contextuales en América Latina
summary: While scholarly attention in Latin America has leaned heavily toward how citizens perceive their legislatures, there is a far more nuanced story to be told about the institutional trust held by the legislators themselves. By diving into 3,362 interviews from the PELA-USAL Project—and employing a multilevel model with multiple imputation—this study moves beyond the usual sociodemographic or partisan explanations to find something more visceral: it is personal ideology, the mirror effect of perceived citizen trust, and the shadow of presiden-tial power that truly define the legislative psyche. Mexico, for its part, sits at a restless midpoint in the region, marked by a polarization that complicates any easy consensus. These findings suggest that we ought to stop viewing institutional trust as a static data point and start seeing it as a living, relational attitude—one deeply entangled with political identity and the shifting scales of power—ultimately forcing a necessary critique of how elites symbolically inhabit the very institutions they represent.

title: Integridad y buen gobierno en las Comunidades Autónomas: el caso de los Fondos Next Generation EU
summary: This article analyzes the challenges faced and the strategies adopted by Spain’s autonomous communities in developing the integrity mechanisms required for the implementation of the Next Generation EU funds. The objective is to examine how they have responded to require-ments concerning anti-fraud efforts, transparency, accountability, and the prevention of conflicts of interest. Using a qualitative approach based on semi-structured interviews with regional officials and documentary analysis of official documents and anti-fraud plans, the study assesses institutional adaptation capacity in a context of multilevel governance and policy transfer.The findings reveal significant heterogeneity in regional responses, shaped by their histo-rical trajectories, institutional capacities, and available resources. Although all communities formally complied with the requirements, effective implementation remains uneven. Most prioritized regulatory responses over deeper institutional transformation. The study identifies patterns of coercive and mimetic isomorphism, where formal compliance tends to prevail over structural change.It concludes that, despite existing constraints, the regions reacted swiftly and effectively. However, the sustainability of progress will depend on their ability to consolidate a genuine culture of integrity beyond mere legal compliance.

title: La obscenidad y sus efectos segregativos, ¿cuerpos sin discursos?
summary: This article examines “The Waldo Moment” Black Mirror, Season Two, Episode Three (Brooker, 2013) to conceptualize contemporary forms of social bonding through a psychoanalytic lens. It argues that political adhesion no longer revolves around the Ideal-ego paradigm but around modalities of jouissance that masquerade as authenticity: insult, obscenity, and the spectacularization of speech. Through the TV debate scene, the screen-van harassment, and the proposal to turn Waldo into a “global platform,” the paper shows how influence becomes quantifiable (views, likes, virality) and how the “advantage” of having no past shields a virtual candidate from biographical challenge. Waldo functions as an object that elicits identification without symbolic mediation, offering a “voice” to the disenchanted and the marginalized, yet fostering communities constituted by rejection rather than shared projects. title: "Soy lo gue digo": Goce e identidad en la era del insulto
summary: This article explores Beef (Netflix, 2023) as a contemporary portrayal of identification processes no longer sustained by Freud’s Ego Ideal, but by a raw, spectacular, and immediate form of jouissance. Drawing on Lacan, Laurent Dupont, and Christiane Alberti, the article examines how the contemporary subject clings to an identity-based certainty that forecloses desire, makes forgiveness impossible, and leaves the body as the only surface on which jouissance is inscribed. Far from moralistic narratives or redemptive arcs, Beef is presented as a tragedy without heroes, where the most moving element is not violence but exhaustion. Within that fatigue of the One, a crack may appear: an empty word that persists, a desire to speak that endures even when language no longer ties. title: Freud y el cine: un encuentro fallido
summary: Since their inception, psychoanalysis and cinema have shared a very particular relationship, in which tension between sympathy and aversion has been the common denominator. title: Desarrollo de una herramienta interactiva en R para el análisis no paramétrico de asociaciones en datos experimentales de ingeniería aplicada
authors: López López, Erika Liliana; Bru Cordero, Osnamir Elías; Correa Álvarez, Cristian David
summary: This article presents a methodological tool designed for the calculation, interpretation, and application of nonparametric association coefficients. The proposal is primarily aimed at researchers and students who need to analyze relationships between variables in contexts where the classical assumptions of normality are not satisfied. In many applied studies, particularly in engineering, education, and the social sciences, researchers frequently work with datasets that exhibit skewness, ties, or outliers, which limits the applicability of traditional parametric techniques. The study includes a conceptual review of the main association coefficients used in nonparametric statistics, including Spearman’s rho, Kendall’s tau, Goodman and Kruskal’s Gamma, Lambda, Cramér’s V, Phi, and Somers’ D. For each of these coefficients, their theoretical foundations and relevant methodological considerations are discussed to support their appropriate use in the analysis of experimental data. As part of the methodological development, these coefficients were implemented in the R programming language, incorporating procedures for statistical estimation, significance testing, and confidence interval calculation. In addition, an interactive application was developed using the Shiny environment, allowing users to upload datasets, identify the type of variables analyzed, select the most appropriate association coefficient, and automatically obtain the analytical results without requiring advanced programming skills. To illustrate the use of the tool, several applied examples are presented in different contexts, including a case study in materials engineering in which the relationship between hardness and wear in metallic components subjected to heat treatment is analyzed. The results show that the choice of association coefficient can significantly influence the interpretation of the data. Overall, the proposed tool facilitates the application of nonparametric methods and contributes to strengthening statistical analysis in scientific research.

title: Petrography and geochemistry of volcanic rocks of the Norean Formation in the Caño Largo Village, municipality of Curumaní-Cesar, Colombia — ES: Petrografía y geoquímica de rocas volcánicas de la Formación Norean en el Pueblo Caño Largo, municipio de Curumaní-Cesar, Colombia
authors: Britto Álvarez, Ricardo Andrés; Morón Soto, Francisco Javier; Lascarro Navarro, Frank David; Rojas Martínez, Elías Ernesto; Manco Jaraba, Dino Carmelo
summary: Near the Caño Largo village, municipality of Curumaní, the Norean Formation consists of a volcanosedimentary sequence composed of dacitic and andesitic volcanic rocks and sandstones. This article aims to elucidate the geochemical and petrographic characteristics of the rocks that make up the Norean Formation in the area. Sampling was carried out randomly with a population of 10 specimens evaluated using X-ray fluorescence (XRF) chemical analysis, and 5 specimens characterized microscopically. The petrographic results established that the rocks are composed of an aphantic matrix with inequigranular porphyritic textures. Mineralogically, they contain quartz, feldspar, plagioclase, hornblende, and chlorite. The geochemical tests were compared with several tectonic discrimination diagrams, determining that the rocks are located in the same crystallization trend, suggesting that they are part of the same magmatic pulse, with SiO2 values ranging from 59.87 wt% to 74.25 wt% (andesites to dacites), formed from a type of calc-alkaline magma in an intraplate orogenic tectonic environment.

title: Incidencia del derretimiento del Nevado El Cocuy sobre la oferta hídrica de las cuencas glaciares
authors: Aponte Ruiz, Manuela; Salazar Ríos, Maria José; Ivanova, Yulia
summary: Colombia is one of the countries with tropical glaciers currently undergoing a melting process as a result of global warming. This is expected to impact the functionality of various ecosystems, as well as the water availability of glacial watersheds. To date, the effect of the melting of the El Cocuy snow-capped mountain on the water supply of the Nevado River—an important source of regional water supply—remains unknown. For this reason, this research employed remote sensing analysis of snow cover through the Normalized Difference Snow Index (NDSI), statistical analysis of hydrological series, and correlation analysis between mean flow rates and the snow-capped area to assess the effect of the mountain’s melting on the water availability of the El Nevado watershed. It was found that the snow-capped mountain is expected to disappear within the next 29 years and that its ablation shows no direct relationship with flow rates. The interannual variation showed that, up until 1998, ablation led to an increase in mean flow values, while its subsequent depletion contributed to a significant decline in the watershed’s water supply. As a result of this process, the average flow of the Nevado River could decrease from 7.32 m³/s to 3.45 m³/s. This highlights the need for urgent medium-term measures for the proper management of water resources to ensure their availability for ecosystems and various socioeconomic uses, where hydrological instrumentation of glacial watersheds is essential and urgent.

summary: The objective of this study was to comparatively analyze the hydraulic efficiency, environmental performance, and mechanical behavior of conventional and modified porous asphalt mixtures. summary: This research presents a material requirements planning (MRP) model using mixed-integer linear programming, with a multi-objective approach, applied to a theoretical bicycle assembly environment. This model is aimed at improving production scheduling in order to ensure demand fulfillment while reducing costs in the production system and maximizing the use of installed capacity. Accordingly, a methodology structured in three phases was adopted. The first consisted of a literature review and formulation of the case study, identifying operational and structural parameters; the second aimed to formulate a compromise-based mixed-integer linear programming model; and, finally, the model was implemented and evaluated in the AMPL IDE environment, using the CPLEX solver. The model proposed in this case study achieved all three key objectives: reducing total costs, minimizing the amount of unmet demand, and maximizing total production over the modeled time horizon (24 weeks). The balanced solution yielded a BALNOR objective value of 0.84; furthermore, 100% demand fulfillment was achieved, with a total production capacity of 4,568 units of finished product. Likewise, total costs were kept at 15,189,080 monetary units. These results validated the model’s applicability as an important decision-support tool in this bicycle assembly context. It is concluded that combining MRP with multi-objective optimization techniques greatly improves system performance, enabling more robust, adaptable, and efficient solutions for organizations.

summary: This study explores how working memory, a key executive function, is activated in children aged 5 to 6 during computational thinking (CT) challenges involving educational robotics. Thematic analysis identified three central categories: the activation of working memory through counting and planning, the use of external elements (mats, body, gestures) as cognitive support, and the limitations observed in the retention and manipulation of information. Likewise, the physical environment and verbal mediation prove essential for sustaining and organizing information during the task. Given the exploratory nature of the study, it is suggested that future research be expanded to different contexts and with various types of scaffolding, in order to gain deeper insight into the development of working memory in technology-based learning environments.

title: ADAT: a tool for assessing computational thinking skills in adults

summary: Computational thinking (CT) is widely recognized as a crucial skill for adults in the digital era. To the best of our knowledge, it represents the first multi-skill CT test adapted for adults in Latin America, addresses a critical gap in population-specific assessment, and informs the design of targeted teaching and learning interventions.

summary: Introduction: in sport, classifying athletes by year of birth during the training period generated inequalities in learning opportunities, a phenomenon known as the Relative Age Effect (RAE). Conclusions: RAE in Spanish elite sport is a predominantly male phenomenon, whose magnitude depends on the interaction between sport and gender rather than on competitive level considered in isolation.

title: Migración y éxodo en Cuba : tendencias migratorias desde el siglo XIX hasta la actualidad
summary: En el presente artículo se explora el contexto histórico de la migración cubana hacia Estados Unidos para analizar el éxodo que se presentó a finales de 2021. El artículo contribuye a una comprensión más profunda del fenómeno migratorio desde un enfoque multidimensional que considera factores políticos, económicos, sociales e históricos.

Conclusion: This study showed that a vegetarian diet, when properly planned, is capable of satisfying the nutritional needs of athletes, ensuring good performance in both strength and endurance.

El objetivo es comprender cómo la escala metropolitana se convierte en un referente clave para evaluar políticas públicas, especialmente en contextos como la Zona Metropolitana del Valle de México (ZMVM), donde movilidad cotidiana, provisión de servicios y gestión del suelo responden a lógicas territoriales que no coinciden con las fronteras político-administrativas. Con un diseño metodológico cualitativo-comparado, basado en análisis documental y normativo de los marcos estatales y federales que regulan la coordinación metropolitana, sumando instrumentos de planeación, financiamiento y gobernanza apoyados en plataformas digitales, datos e información territorial, estos insumos permiten analizar la cartografía y caracterización socioespacial, la expansión urbana, distribución poblacional y flujos intermunicipales junto al caso del estado de Hidalgo, parte de ZMVM, donde se aplican entrevistas semiestructuradas con actores gubernamentales, encuesta de movilidad con cuestionario abierto a la población y revisión de experiencias de coordinación intergubernamental. Los hallazgos preliminares muestran que la metrópoli redefine el diagnóstico de problemas públicos reconfigurando capacidades estatales, tensiones autonomía territorial-interdependencia gubernamental y responsabilidad con la población que afectan las dinámicas educativas y económicas. Se concluye que avanzar hacia una gobernanza metropolitana exige fortalecer mecanismos de coordinación vinculante, integrar criterios territoriales en las políticas y que población y territorio orienten la acción pública. Se esperan resultados de la encuesta en Hidalgo para profundizar el análisis.

title: Inteligencia emocional y su relación con el clima escolar en estudiantes de una institución educativa privada de Villa el Salvador, Perú
authors: Paredes Mendoz, Leonela Estefanía a; Huayhua Gutierrez, Flavia Teresa; Espinoza Sotelo, Joan Carlos
summary: This study aimed to determine the relationship between emotional intelligence and school climate among students at a private educational institution in Villa El Salvador, Peru. A quantitative, basic, correlational, non-experimental, and cross-sectional study was conducted. Using non-probability sampling, 142 students aged 12 to 15 years and enrolled in the first through third grades of secondary school were selected. The 24-item Trait Meta-Mood Scale, which assesses emotional attention, clarity, and repair, and the Moos School Social Climate Scale were administered. Data were processed using SPSS version 25 and analyzed with Spearman’s rho correlation coefficient. No statistically significant relationship was found between emotional intelligence and school climate (ρ = .046, p = .583). Likewise, no significant associations were identified between school climate and emotional attention (ρ = −.072, p = .392), emotional repair (ρ = .103, p = .223), or emotional clarity (ρ = .103, p = .223). In the sample examined, no evidence of an association between perceived emotional intelligence and school climate was found. The findings suggest that other personal, family, and institutional variables should be examined, while considering the limitations associated with non-probability sampling, the use of self-report measures, and the inclusion of a single educational institution.

title: Pautas estratégicas para la mejora de la experiencia turística en el destino Topes de Collantes, Cuba
authors: Rodríguez Rodríguez, Amelia; Acosta Mesa, Sandro Felipe; Robert-Beatón, Martha Omara
summary: This study proposes strategic guidelines aimed at improving the tourist experience in the destination of Topes de Collantes, Cuba. A mixed-methods research design was adopted. Reviews published on TripAdvisor between 2004 and 2025 were analyzed: 6,120 corresponding to the Viñales Valley and 518 to Topes de Collantes. Natural language processing techniques, sentiment analysis, descriptive statistics, and a Pareto chart were applied. The findings were triangulated through a literature review and a brainstorming session with specialists from Cuba’s Sectoral Tourism Program. Topes de Collantes showed a lower relative presence of online reviews and a smaller proportion of positive ratings than Viñales. The main aspects associated with dissatisfaction were the perceived loss of authenticity, value for money, insufficient information on services and prices, limited diversification of the tourism offer, and accessibility difficulties, especially during the rainy season. Based on these findings, twenty strategic guidelines were developed, focusing on cultural authenticity, service quality, tourism communication, product diversification, and connectivity. It is concluded that the proposed guidelines may guide destination management toward a more sustainable, accessible tourism offer aligned with visitors’ expressed perceptions.

title: Protección animal en el Ecuador desde el análisis normativo y jurisprudencial en el marco de los derechos de la naturaleza
authors: Silva Andrade, Guido Javier; Calderón Velásquez, María José; Marfetán Marfetán, Viviana Del Rocío; Fernández Andrade, Luis Gabriel
summary: The recognition of the rights of nature in the Ecuadorian Constitution marked a shift toward an ecocentric approach and has generated debate regarding the legal status of animals as subjects of rights. The objective of this study was to critically examine, from a normative and jurisprudential perspective, the current state of animal protection in Ecuador. A documentary research methodology was employed, based on the analysis of constitutional provisions, secondary legislation, and judicial decisions, using inductive-deductive and exegetical-analytical methods. It was determined that Ecuador recognizes nature as a subject of rights; however, it does not explicitly establish animals as individual rights-bearing entities. Their protection derives from environmental and criminal norms, as well as from judicial interpretations. Limitations persist, including normative dispersion, lack of conceptual clarity, and weak protection of domestic animals. Animal protection in Ecuador remains indirect and insufficient. Greater normative harmonization, explicit recognition of animals as subjects of rights, and institutional strengthening are required to ensure effective protection.

title: La festividad del Pawkar Raymi y su papel en la preservación de las tradiciones indígenas andinas
authors: Jaramillo Burgos, Manuel Fernando; Chávez Fonseca, Lila Galicia; Tello Velasteguí, Adriano Israel
summary: Ecuador’s cultural and ethnic diversity is one of the fundamental pillars of its national identity. The study aimed to analyze the role of the Pawkar Raymi festival in the preservation of traditions, the transmission of ancestral knowledge, and the construction of cultural identity in Andean Indigenous communities in the province of Chimborazo, Ecuador. A qualitative approach was adopted, with an ethnographic design and a descriptive-interpretative scope. The research was conducted in Indigenous communities in Chimborazo province using purposive sampling. Data collection techniques included participant observation, semi-structured interviews, and field notes, aimed at identifying ritual practices, sociocultural dynamics, and community perceptions. Pawkar Raymi is configured as a cyclical ritual system that articulates symbolic, agricultural, and spiritual dimensions. Practices such as the Tumarina and the pampamesa demonstrate its role in spiritual purification, social cohesion, and the intergenerational transmission of knowledge. Additionally, processes of adaptation in urban contexts and the incorporation of contemporary elements were identified, generating dynamics of cultural re-signification. The festival constitutes a mechanism for cultural preservation and collective identity. However, it faces challenges derived from globalization, migration, and generational distancing. In this context, strategies such as intercultural education, cultural tourism, and the use of digital technologies emerge as relevant tools for its strengthening and continuity.

summary: The management of academic quality processes in Higher Education Institutions requires Strategic Information Systems (SIS) grounded in rigorous theoretical and methodological foundations, capable of ensuring relevant and reliable information for decision-making and continuous improvement. This proposal aligns with USGP’s institutional commitment to the continuous improvement of academic quality management.

title: Régimen de curaduría de bienes en menores de edad en Ecuador: fundamentos jurídicos y limitaciones en su implementación
authors: Chugá Quemac, Rosa Evelyn; Puetate Paucar, Jairo Mauricio; Dávila Castillo, Marcelo Raúl
summary: The curatorship of assets for minors constitutes an essential legal mechanism for the protection of property in contexts of legal incapacity. The objective of this study was to examine the structural weaknesses of the system of asset curatorship for minors in Ecuador. To this end, a qualitative approach was employed, based on a doctrinal and legal-normative design. A review of primary legal sources, specialized doctrine, and relevant case law was conducted through interpretative and thematic analysis. The study revealed that, although the legal framework establishes clear functions, responsibilities, and restrictions for the curator, there are gaps in terms of institutional oversight, training, and supervision mechanisms. Case law shows a tendency to expand the scope of curatorship, incorporating psychosocial criteria into the protection of the minor. Structural weaknesses were identified in the implementation of the system, particularly in oversight and the training of curators. In response, a training program is proposed to strengthen technical and ethical competencies, contributing to more efficient, transparent management aligned with the principle of the best interests of the child.

title: Factores asociados a la caries dental en estudiantes universitarios: un análisis mediante Mapas Cognitivos Difusos
authors: Rodríguez Lasluisa, Danilo Enrique; Pilco Viteri, Justine Daniela; Guedez Mujica, Ana Graciela
summary: Dental caries represents a significant public health problem among young people, particularly during transitional stages such as entry into higher education, where self-care habits may be affected. The aim of this study was to identify the factors influencing the development of dental caries in students aged 17 to 19 enrolled in the propedeutic B program at the Universidad Regional Autónoma de los Andes (UNIANDES). A qualitative study was conducted using Fuzzy Cognitive Maps (FCMs), with a phenomenological design and an intentional sample of 10 students. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis. Subsequently, FCMs were applied to model the relationships among the identified factors and to determine their level of influence. The findings revealed a discrepancy between theoretical knowledge and preventive practices. Although students recognize appropriate hygiene and dietary habits, they exhibit inconsistent behaviors, such as sporadic dental visits and self-medication. The FCM analysis identified preventive awareness, motivation to visit the dentist, and frequency of visits as the most influential factors, forming an interdependent system of variables. The occurrence of dental caries in this population reflects a multifactorial dynamic in which knowledge alone does not ensure healthy behaviors. Comprehensive strategies focused on behavioral change, motivation, and access to services are required to promote a preventive culture in oral health.

title: Challenges of pharmacological treatment for leprosy: a systematic review
authors: Alejandro, Carlos R.; Galarza López, Judith; Díaz Contino, Cindy Giselle; Loor Vinces, Lester Willian; Cdiaz, Cdiaz
summary: Leprosy is a chronic, transmissible infectious disease of ancient origin that primarily affects the skin, mucous membranes, and peripheral nerves, potentially leading to disability and death. Despite advances achieved through multidrug therapy (MDT), deficiencies in public health systems persist, particularly in developing countries. The aim of the present study is to identify the achievements and challenges of pharmacological treatment for leprosy in order to advance toward its eradication. A systematic literature review was conducted following the PRISMA methodology, using searches in the scientific databases PubMed and Web of Science, and selecting studies published between 2020 and 2025 related to the pharmacological treatment of leprosy. A total of 18 studies were analyzed, addressing current treatment approaches, management in specific cases, and both challenges and advances in pharmacological therapy. The findings indicate that, although MDT remains the treatment of choice and is effective for leprosy, significant weaknesses in health systems persist, leading to difficulties in the acquisition of medications, limited accessibility to health services, delayed diagnosis, and poor treatment adherence.

title: Alcances y limitaciones epistemológicas de la inferencia estadística contemporánea: una revisión sistemática
authors: Villavicencio Cedeño, Lissette Beatriz; Batista Garcet, Yoiler; Tenelenda Cudco, Sandra; Guanga Chunata, Deysi Margoth; Casaliglla Ger, Darwin
summary: Statistical inference is fundamental to producing scientific knowledge, interpreting evidence, and guiding decision-making under uncertainty. However, its validity depends on study design, underlying assumptions, analytical transparency, and the appropriate interpretation of results. The objective of this study was to qualitatively synthesize the epistemological scope and limitations attributed to statistical inference in recent scientific literature. A qualitative systematic review guided by PRISMA 2020 was conducted. The PubMed and Europe PMC databases were searched to identify publications issued between 2021 and 2025. Thirteen studies were included and analyzed through a thematic, comparative, and interpretive synthesis. The results were organized into five themes: reinterpretation of the p-value and intervals as measures of compatibility; coexistence of frequentist and Bayesian approaches; reproducibility and quality of statistical reporting; uncertainty quantification in artificial intelligence; and the relationship between causal inference and machine learning. The reviewed literature questions dichotomous decisions based exclusively on statistical significance and emphasizes the need to consider effect sizes, assumptions, context, and practical relevance. It also indicates that inferential validity is shaped by institutional practices, transparency, and study design quality. The study concludes that statistical inference remains essential to scientific reasoning but does not provide definitive certainty. Its rigorous use requires making assumptions explicit, calibrating uncertainty, ensuring analytical transparency, and clearly distinguishing among association, prediction, and causality.

summary: The term « fantasy » (Greek: phantasma), refers both to a ghost and a visual hal-lucination. In this context, it is less about a visual representation than about the expression of an action, the experience of its fulfillment, encompassing all the outlined trajectories and the human sensations thereby produced. In other words, fantasy arises the moment an image is created. We will consider the image not as the visual representation of a scenario, but as the exercise, expression, revelation, and/or reproduction of a sensory perception. This paper explores how the disruption of the sense of sight, essential to the construction of fantasy in Belle de Jour, is counteracted by the en-actment of a new experimental technique of observation, materialized through the sense of hearing. In this way, we propose a possible interpretation of a sensory cartography of fantasy, wherein the gaze is diffracted inward, toward an inner eye and activated by an internal rhythm. Our analysis traces a sensory technique for expressing fantasy, marked by a diversion from the primary uses of sight and hearing. We will thus demonstrate that when direct visual confrontation fails, the character transcends it through a lateral gaze and the creation of a personal surveillance chamber. We will then show how listening becomes crucial, ultimately giving rise to an internal rhythm that enables the opening of the gaze.
