title: Assessing the Efficacy of Kinect-Based Educational Gaming on Primary School Cognitive and Motor Development
summary: Introduction: Motion-based educational technologies have gained relevance because of their potential to integrate body movement, digital interaction, and gamified learning. The intervention was organized into four stages: interactive board engagement, postural and lateral coordination, short-trajectory obstacle navigation, and guided long-distance movements. Results: The results show favorable performance in motor accuracy, lateral coordination, sequence following, and movement-based problem solving. title: Transperientiality in Teacher Training: A Transcomplex Shift Towards Nonlinear Learning Trajectories
authors: Cabral Mier, Oscar Ernesto; Cabral García, Gabriel; Loera Serrano, Selso; Duenas Luna, Mary Victoria
summary: Introduction: Initial teacher education currently takes place within educational contexts characterized by complexity, diversity, and uncertainty, revealing the limitations of traditional linear and prescriptive models for explaining how future teachers actually learn. Although contemporary theories have substantially expanded the understanding of professional learning, they continue to address experience, reflection, participation, competencies, and identity as relatively isolated dimensions. This article introduces Transperientiality as an emerging transcomplex analytical framework capable of explaining nonlinear learning trajectories through the recursive integration of lived experience, professional identity, context, and pedagogical knowledge. Method: The study adopts a theoretical-conceptual design grounded in a qualitative, hermeneutic, and transcomplex perspective. Through critical analysis and interpretive systematization of specialized literature, the research establishes a dialogue between Complex Thinking, Transcomplexity, and Transdisciplinarity, drawing primarily on the contributions of Morin, Nicolescu, Villegas, and related scholars. The analysis followed a recursive process of conceptual identification, comparative interpretation, and theoretical synthesis to construct Transperientiality as an autonomous analytical category. Results: The analysis identifies an important epistemological gap in current teacher learning theories, which insufficiently explain how heterogeneous experiences recursively reshape professional identity across nonlinear trajectories. In response, Transperientiality is conceptualized as an ontological and transcomplex framework that positions lived experience as the central structure through which teacher learning is continuously reconfigured. This perspective integrates cognitive, emotional, ethical, contextual, and identity dimensions into a dynamic explanatory model that broadens the understanding of professional learning, particularly within the diverse educational contexts of Mexican Normal Schools, while offering broader international relevance. Conclusions: Transperientiality represents an original theoretical contribution to teacher education by shifting the analytical focus from experience as a pedagogical resource to experience as an ontological condition of becoming a teacher. This epistemological shift provides a more comprehensive understanding of nonlinear learning trajectories and offers conceptual foundations for rethinking curriculum design, pedagogical practice, educational assessment, and future empirical research from a transcomplex perspective.

title: An AI Chatbot in the Reduction of Anxiety in a Community Mental Health Center
authors: Molina Martinez, Fiorella Alejandra; Garcia Martinez, Gonzalo Enrique
summary: Introduction: Anxiety is one of the fastest-growing mental health problems worldwide. In this context, digital tools may help improve access to mental health support, especially in underserved communities or peri-urban settlements with limited access to healthcare services. Method: quasi-experimental single-arm pre–post study was conducted with 30 adults presenting anxiety symptoms who used an emotional support chatbot for six weeks. Anxiety was assessed before and after the intervention using the Zung Self-Rating Anxiety Scale, and usability was measured with the System Usability Scale (SUS). Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, percentages, and 95% confidence intervals) were calculated. Pre–post differences were analyzed using a paired-samples t-test with effect size estimation (Cohen’s dz). Internal consistency was examined using Cronbach’s alpha. Open-ended responses were analyzed through thematic review and word-frequency analysis. Results: Before the intervention, 36.7% of participants presented with severe anxiety, 30.0% with mild anxiety, 20.0% with moderate anxiety, and 13.3% with normal levels. After the intervention, 53.3% reached normal levels of anxiety, while severe and moderate cases decreased to 16.7% and 13.3%, respectively. The overall reduction in anxiety symptoms was 50%. Regarding usability, the system was mostly rated as acceptable to excellent. Conclusions: The Florence AI chatbot was associated with reductions in self-reported anxiety symptoms and was generally perceived as an accessible and acceptable source of emotional support among adults receiving care in a community mental health setting. However, because of the single-arm design, small sample size, and gender imbalance, these findings should be interpreted as preliminary associations rather than evidence of efficacy. Larger controlled studies with longer follow-up periods are needed to determine the effectiveness, safety, and generalizability of AI-based emotional support interventions.

title: Aproximación bibliométrica de la producción historiográfica mundial sobre Centroamérica contemporánea, 1970-2021
authors: Jimenez Alvarez, Carlos Josue; Ramírez Roldán, José David
summary: This article presents a bibliometric analysis of worldwide historiographical production on Central America as a region between 1970 and 2021, with the aim of identifying trends, ruptures, and moments of consolidation in the construction of a regional history of the isthmus. The research is based on a descriptive study of 117 academic publications, identified through a systematic search of specialized databases and academic catalogs. Based on this sample, the thematic evolution and methodological and theoretical changes in the field are examined. The analysis was conducted using techniques of thematic classification, historical periodization, and quantitative comparison of historiographical output, which allowed for structuring its development into four stages: background, ruptures, and professionalization up to 1985; a surge in intellectual effervescence between 1986 and 1999; renewal and new interpretations between 2000 and 2013; and the consolidation of regional historiography between 2014 and 2021. The results show that political-military contexts, academic institutionalization, and the participation of national and international researchers were decisive in the transition from nationalist approaches toward more pluralistic regional perspectives, culminating in the incorporation of approaches such as entangled history. Overall, the study offers a comprehensive view of the professionalization and maturation of Central American historiography.

title: Reconstrucción del ligamento cruzado anterior con tendón rotuliano: Evaluación de más de 2 años de seguimiento
summary: The results of 2 years research based on 142 anterior cruciate ligament reconstructions using bone-patellar tendon-bone as a graft, were analyzed. The global results showed that 81% had a normal knee (A) or almost normal (B), according to IKDC. With the Cincinati test, 82% were between excellent and good. Apart from the global evaluation, it was also analyzed how the meniscus and the articular cartilage conditions reacted to and influenced the final result by dividing the patients, in five groups: under 30, over 30, patients with 2 to 5 years from surgery, 5 to 7 years and more than 7 years from surgery. title: Lesiones metastásicas de los huesos largos
summary: Retrospective review of 42 long bone metastatic lesions in 35 patients treated surgically between 1992-1998; 21 patients were female and 14 male; 25 lesions were treated for established pathologic fractures, while the remaining 17 were stabilized for impending pathologic fractures. Average age was 63.7 years (42-80). The most common primary tumors were breast, kidney, lung, prostate and thyroid. Internal fixation was enhanced with methylmetacrilate in 33 lesions (78.5%). Postoperative radiotherapy was used in all cases. Life expectancy varied according to the primary lesions (74% at 2 years for breast and prostate); 33 patients (94.2%) returned to their preoperative status. Postoperative complications were reported in 6 patients (17.1%), and included failure of fixation in 3 cases, deep infection 1 case, 1 thromboembolic complication, and deep vein thrombosis in one case. Failure of internal fixation (3 cases) occurred 1 year after the original surgery, and was directly related to a longer survival rate and progression of the original disease. Most patients will benefit from a timely and adequate surgical treatment. It is functionally better and involves less morbidity to stabilize a bone before a pathologic fracture occurs. The fixation device should provide the best stability in a definitive way. Osteosynthesis enhancement with cement improves the stability of the construct. We prefer the use of intramedulary nails to plates for diaphyseal injuries due to the high complication rate in our series. Even though there was no difference in our series in osteosynthesis versus total joint replacement in próxima! and dista! long bone lesions, the literature shows a smaller complication rate with arthroplasty. Radiotherapy is an important adjuvant for the treatment of long bone metástasis.

summary: Intimate partner violence (IPV) in the LGBTQIA+ population appears to be exacerbated by minority stressors. A theoretical model that takes into account effects of different factors, and their interactions, on the development of sexual orientation was used as reference. A scoping review was carried out, based on PRISMA-ScR, with searches made in SCOPUS, PubMed, PsycINFO and SciELO. title: La construcción del Estado administrativo (y del derecho administrativo como ciencia autónoma) en Italia
summary: This essay examines the social, economic, and legal transformations that took place in Europe during the 18th and 19th centuries, which laid the foundations for the development of the administrative state. It focuses on the development of the administrative state in Italy during the 19th century, from the adoption of the Napoleonic model by the states prior to unification, to the significant continuity between the Kingdom of Sardinia and the Kingdom of Italy. The central part of the essay is devoted to the pivotal thirty-year period from 1885 to 1915, characterised by significant changes in industrial, technological, and socio-economic spheres. The reforms implemented by the Crispi and Giolitti governments were instrumental in the rapid development of the administrative state. The pivotal role of the bureaucratic apparatus also sparked a radical cultural shift in the humanities, resulting in the emergence of administrative law as an independent discipline within the legal sphere. During this period, Italian administrative law developed under the guidance of Vittorio Emanuele Orlando and the theories of Oreste Ranelletti, Federico Cammeo and Santi Romano. This evolutionary trajectory enabled Italy to achieve two objectives: firstly, a social policy objective of preserving the unity of the state and the leading role of the upper-middle class; and secondly, a legal policy objective of affirming the autonomy of a new field of legal studies. At this historic juncture, the Italian school of public law emerged as a political instrument for realising a specific project of national unity and identity focused on the administrative state.

On this basis, the study analyses the jurisdictional, procedural and doctrinal implications of the ruling and offers a critical assessment of its impact on the Spanish system of public contracting.

summary: This article analyses the emergence and development of regulatory sandboxes in Spain in the context of deep changes in the modern Administrative Law. The study situates sandboxes primarily within the context of the evolution of the regulatory state and the growing need for institutional learning in environments characterised by technological complexity and information asymmetries between regulators and regulated entities. Within this framework, testing environments can facilitate responsible innovation and uphold the constitutional principle of good governance by improving regulatory knowledge, enabling regulatory learning and strengthening evidence-based policy-making. However, this very interaction between regulators and private actors also entails risks, including regulatory capture, distortions of competition and a lack of transparency. The article then examines the current legal framework governing testing environments in Spain at three levels: national, regional and local. Finally, the article concludes that, whilst regulatory sandboxes can be valuable tools for innovation and regulatory learning, the Spanish legal framework would benefit from greater coordination, clearer governance mechanisms and stronger safeguards to ensure that experimentation remains consistent with the principles of the rule of law.

title: La carga mental y la hiperconexión digital como riesgo psicosocial emergente mental
summary: The paper analyzes digital mental load and overconnection as psychosocial risks that today are at the center of preventive duty and the organization of working time. Based on Article 40.2 of the Spanish Constitution and the regulation of the Workers’ Statute, it argues that digitalization and teleworking are blurring the traditional boundaries of working hours and rest, with a direct impact on health. LTD strengthens the requirement for protection equivalent to that in face-to-face work and fully projects the safety duty of the Occupational Risk Prevention Law, obliging the assessment and management of organizational and psychosocial risks, not just ergonomic ones. In remote work, prevention shifts from controlling the physical space to analyzing organization: communication rhythms, availability times, response pressure, and technological interruptions. Recent case law consolidates a material view of psychosocial assessment and links digital disconnection with the effective protection of rest and mental health. Finally, business responsibilities (administrative, civil, and even criminal) are examined, and the need to integrate digital indicators into the assessment is highlighted.

title: Cómo se proyectan en la práctica los ajustes razonables
summary: The recent reform of the termination of employment contracts on grounds of a declaration of permanent total disability, insofar as it now requires the prior adoption of reasonable accommodations, has erred by being overly terse and overly generic with respect to crucial concepts. Indeed, it offers nothing new as to what is to be understood by “reasonable accommodation”, nor does it establish, for all cases, a clear threshold delimiting when these measures aimed at preserving the employment contract of an employee who has subsequently become disabled would begin to constitute an “undue burden”. This places legal practitioners in situations of uncertainty that would have been easy to avoid. The same applies to companies and their occupational risk prevention services, to which the aforementioned provision entrusts the design and implementation of these measures. In the absence of any regulatory guidance, prevention services are extrapolating the procedure provided for situations involving risk during pregnancy. This is a three-tier, step-by-step procedure: adaptation of the original job position, reassignment to another vacant position compatible with the worker’s new condition, or termination of the contract. On the other hand, the fact that the legislature imposes on companies the obligation to undertake reasonable accommodations even in cases of permanent absolute disability and severe disability appears ineffective and excessive.

summary: Flexion-distraction injuries of the thoracolumbar spine are infrequent because of their special production mechanism. In such lesions, surgery is indicated in the presence of mechanical or neurological instability, or when patients are unable to undergo conservative treatment. Open reduction and posterior spinal fusion is the recommended surgery. The functional outcome was excellent in 5 patients and good in 1 according to the Chan scale.

summary: Acute muscle lesions have been cited as the most common injury in competitive athletes. Despite their common occurrence there are relatively few studies that investigate these injuries. The purpose of this paper is to analyze a group of patients with clinically diagnosed acute muscle lesion, presenting a normal ultrasound and an MRI showing the injury. title: Brechas rurales en la Política Nacional de Confianza y Seguridad Digital de Colombia: un análisis comparativo con la Guía UIT 2021 y propuesta de un Índice de Vulnerabilidad Cibernética Rural (IVCR)
authors: Sánchez Suárez, Gabriel; Medina Delgado, Byron
summary: CONPES 3995 and the National Digital Security Strategy 2025-2027 relegate structural vulnerabilities of rural Colombia, omitting radio spectrum underutilization, institutional weakness, digital illiteracy, and connectivity deficits. title: Reconocimiento facial aplicado a la gestión en instituciones educativas: una revisión sistemática de literatura
authors: Zamora Noriega, Miller Joel; Fernández Carrión, Nixon Omar
summary: Facial recognition has been rapidly incorporated into the management of educational institutions, yet evidence on its performance and conditions of use remains scattered. This systematic review, conducted under the PRISMA 2020 protocol, analyses 25 open-access articles published between 2020 and 2025 in Scopus, ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore and Springer Nature Link, selected from 6,999 initial records. Applications concentrate on attendance control (44%) and access control (40%), followed by cognitive monitoring (12%) and biometric security (4%). The ResNet/FaceNet family is the most widely used (28% of studies) and reported accuracies exceed 90% in most implementations, although they derive from controlled settings with small samples. The review identifies three critical gaps: no study documents informed consent procedures, none describes the demographic composition of its datasets, and only one empirically assesses user acceptance. We conclude that the technical maturity of the technology outpaces its ethical and regulatory maturity, so institutional adoption requires demographic audits, explicit biometric data protection policies and multi-stakeholder acceptance studies.

title: El viejo Atlántico negro: solidaridad, agencia periférica y razón de estado en la política exterior cubana hacia África: el caso de Angola
summary: This article analyses the Cuban intervention in Angola during the Cold War as a practice of state-led and co-produced internationalism. Against interpretations that have reduced it to an expression of revolutionary solidarity, subordination to Soviet strategy, or an autonomous assertion by Havana, the article situates it within an asymmetric coalition in which Cuba, the MPLA, the Angolan state, the Soviet Union, South Africa, and various liberation movements in Southern Africa converged. Drawing on a critical and interpretive review of the historiography on Cuban foreign policy, the Angolan conflict, and the Cold War in Southern Africa, the article examines the African requests and strategies that shaped the intervention, the material and geopolitical constraints that limited Cuban action, and the military, diplomatic, and symbolic effects of the Cuban presence in Angola. The central argument is that peripheral agency operated as a relational, situated, and negotiated practice. Solidarity, raison d’état, and material dependence did not function as mutually exclusive logics, as they constituted intertwined dimensions of the same historical process.

title: Detection of flowering in pineapple (Ananas comosus) using deep learning and drone technology
authors: López Canteñs, Gilberto; Martinez Nicolas, Carlos; Velazquez Lopez, Noe; López Cruz, Irineo L.
summary: Aim of study: Identifying flowering in pineapples is critical for the selective application of growth regulators and for achieving a uniform harvest. summary: This study aimed to evaluate the physiological, behavioral, and productive responses of goat kids and lambs to zootechnical management practices – specifically navel healing and ear tagging – using infrared thermography (IRT) as a non-invasive diagnostic tool. Ear tagging was conducted on the third day using earrings and assessed using IRT at several intervals (1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 30, and 60 days after the earring application). Lambs exhibited higher weight gain from day 30 onwards, potentially due to lower physiological stress. Goat kids showed higher temperatures and frequency of vocalization responses than lambs, highlighting the need for species-specific welfare considerations in livestock practices.

title: Dipteran abundance and family richness across different olive landscape contexts
summary: Landscape complexity favours the abundance and richness of several groups of beneficial arthropods in olive groves while reducing the abundance of pest insects. In addition to beneficial or harmful dipterans, canopy-dwelling flies in olive groves play a role in the sustainability of the agroecosystem by providing alternative prey to important predators. The abundance and family richness of dipterans were studied in the olive-growing area of south-eastern Madrid, Spain, across 15 olive groves representing a gradient of landscape complexity. Dipterans were sampled during the early summer of two years using yellow sticky traps, and the landscape structure was characterised using composition and configuration indices, which were calculated with Fragstats in ArcGIS. Dipterans belonging to 32 families were recorded, with Chloropidae and Sciaridae being the most abundant. Some families with predatory or parasitoid behaviour were also recorded. No strong landscape effects were detected. The area of the olive groves had a slight negative effect on both the abundance and family richness of Diptera. However, a negative effect of Shannon’s evenness index was observed. Thus, Dipteran populations in olive canopies appear to be relatively stable across different landscape contexts. This presence of alternative prey contributes to biological control, thereby enhancing the resilience of the agroecosystem.

title: Effects of phenolic-standardized Crataegus orientalis flower extract on honey bee colony development and seasonal honey yield
summary: Objetivo del estudio: Evaluar los efectos de un extracto floral de Crataegus orientalis Pall. estandarizado en contenido fenólico sobre el desarrollo de colonias de abejas melíferas y el rendimiento de miel al final de la temporada, así como determinar si una suplementación de corta duración al inicio de la primavera produce efectos persistentes a nivel de colonia bajo condiciones de campo. Área de estudio: El estudio se llevó a cabo durante la temporada apícola de 2025 en el apiario del Centro de Aplicación e Investigación Apícola de la Universidad de Bayburt, ubicado en el noreste de Türkiye. Materiales y métodos: Se utilizaron veinticuatro colonias de abejas melíferas (Apis mellifera L.) inicialmente equilibradas, que se distribuyeron aleatoriamente en cuatro grupos (n = 6): un grupo control alimentado con jarabe de sacarosa:agua (1:1) y tres grupos tratados con 50, 100 y 200 mg GAE L⁻¹ de extracto floral de Crataegus orientalis estandarizado en compuestos fenólicos. Las colonias se alimentaron diariamente durante 21 días a comienzos de la primavera y se monitorizaron en siete momentos (T0–T6) desde mediados de mayo hasta finales de agosto. El desarrollo colonial se evaluó mediante el área de cría (cm²) y el número de cuadros con abejas, mientras que el número de abejas muertas en la entrada de la colmena se registró como indicador de seguridad. El rendimiento neto de miel se determinó al final de la temporada. Resultados principales: El consumo diario de jarabe no difirió entre los grupos (P > 0.05), mientras que la ingesta diaria de compuestos fenólicos aumentó de manera dependiente de la dosis (P < 0.05). El área de cría se incrementó significativamente con la dosis y fue mayor en el grupo de dosis alta en comparación con el grupo control durante toda la temporada (P < 0.001). No se observaron diferencias significativas entre los grupos en cuanto al número de cuadros con abejas ni al índice de mortalidad (P > 0.05). El rendimiento neto de miel al final de la temporada fue significativamente mayor en el grupo de dosis alta que en el grupo control (P < 0.01). Aspectos destacados de la investigación: La suplementación de corta duración al inicio de la primavera con extracto floral de Crataegus orientalis estandarizado en compuestos fenólicos favoreció el desarrollo de la cría sin incrementar la mortalidad de las abejas adultas. Esta ventaja temprana en el desarrollo se tradujo en una mejora medible del rendimiento de miel al final de la temporada bajo condiciones de campo.

summary: Aim of study: To optimize seed spacing and organic growing media combinations to enhance uniform germination, seedling vigor, and the proportion of graftable seedlings in Prunus armeniaca (apricot). Area of study: The study site is situated in the mid-hill region of the North-Western Himalayas, Experimental Nursery of Dr. Yashwant Singh Parmar University of Horticulture and Forestry, Nauni, Solan, Himachal Pradesh, India. Material and methods: A factorial experiment was conducted using three intra-row seed spacings (S1: 15 cm × 5 cm, S2: 15 cm × 10 cm, S3: 15 cm × 15 cm) and five organic growing media (M1: Cocopeat; M2: Sand; M3: Cocopeat + FYM (farmyard manure) in 1:1 ratio; M4: FYM; M5: Sand + FYM in 1:1 ratio). Pearson correlation analysis was conducted to examine relationships among variables. Main results: The S3M3 treatment (15 cm × 15 cm with cocopeat + FYM) produced the highest germination percentage (81.21%), sturdiness quotient (19.93), and graftable seedling proportion (85.55%). Wider spacing significantly improved vegetative and physiological traits. Growing media with higher organic content positively influenced root weight and seedling vigor, though negatively correlated with total root length, indicating a trade-off between elongation and biomass accumulation. Research highlights: Spatial configuration and substrate optimization are critical for improving seedling quality traits essential for grafting and successful field establishment. The combination of wider spacing (15 cm × 15 cm) and cocopeat + FYM (1:1) is recommended for nursery protocols to enhance apricot propagation efficiency in temperate agro-ecologies.

title: Mercedes Sosa y la decolonialidad: género, raza y clase en su obra musical
summary: This study analyzes the musical work of Mercedes Sosa from a decolonial perspective, based on the hypothesis that her South American mestiza voice constitutes a counter-hegemonic tool. The study was conducted through a literature review of academic scholarship on Mercedes Sosa. Based on this review, a decolonial and intersectional feminist approach was adopted to examine how the vocal and symbolic performance of the artist contributes to the revaluation of historically silenced forms of knowledge and the resignification of marginalized identities. The results indicate that her artistic work operates as a sensitive pedagogy of liberation and promotes forms of symbolic resistance to colonial structures. The study concludes that the work of Mercedes Sosa challenges hierarchies inherited from coloniality and opens possibilities for the construction of emancipatory epistemological projects within the Latin American context.

authors: Jara Ibarra, Camila; Sánchez Bachmann, Macarena; Martin Guichou, Lucas; Romo Sácnhez, Javiera
summary: A consistent gender gap in political participation favors men. Its origin is identified in political socialization during the school period. Objective: to examine the relationship between political ambition and civic education, with particular attention to gender gaps among secondary students in Chile. Methodology: data came from the Gender and Citizenship Survey (n = 698), administered to students in their second to last year of secondary education. The analysis considers nascent political ambition, both at the level of professional aspirations and within schools, alongside individual dispositions regarding civic education, academic self-esteem, and political voice. title: Análisis sistémico y modelación estructural de la crisis fiscal regional y nacional en Bolivia: propuesta de resiliencia y diversificación desde la Universidad Evangélica Boliviana — ES: sistémico y modelación estructural de la crisis fiscal regional y nacional en Bolivia: propuesta de resiliencia y diversificación desde la Universidad Evangélica Boliviana
authors: Vera, Roberto Carlos; Salas Peña, Mauricio Alejandro; Caballero Saavedra, Caril Ivanna; Paniagua Arandia, Israel; Alberti Uzqueda, José Antonio
summary: La crisis fiscal que atraviesa Bolivia en el periodo 2024-2025, no constituye un fenómeno coyuntural transitorio, sino se evidencia la manifestación de un colapso sistémico inherente al modelo extractivo-rentista de financiamiento público. Bajo un enfoque de la Dinámica de Sistemas Complejos, este estudio modela el comportamiento de las finanzas públicas del departamento de Santa Cruz y de las Entidades Territoriales Autónomas (ETAs) de Bolivia como un Sistema Adaptativo Complejo, caracterizado por bucles de realimentación reforzadores, retardados temporales y comportamientos no lineales. La metodología se fundamentó en la formulación de un modelo físico dinámico de ecuaciones diferenciales stock-flujo, calibrado con la información presupuestaria y macroeconómica de fuentes oficiales y privadas (2014-2025). Los resultados demuestran que el acelerado agotamiento de las reservas de gas natural ha desencadenado una trampa de sobreendeudamiento; en el Municipio de Santa Cruz de la Sierra, el servicio de la deuda (1.019 M Bs en 2025) absorbe el 75,4% de sus ingresos propios, superando 2,7 veces la inversión pública combinada de los seis municipios metropolitanos. En las conclusiones se sintetiza la simulación que evidencia un punto de bifurcación crítica hacia 2027 bajo el escenario tendencial evaluado como alternativa al rescate fiscal convencional, se demuestra que un cambio en la topología del sistema genera un bucle reforzador en la productividad que estabiliza la trayectoria fiscal e incrementa la resiliencia económica nacional.

title: Evaluación multidimensional de la salud familiar en Santa Marta, Colombia
authors: Jiménez Villamizar, María Paola; Vargas Roncallo, Jorge Andrés; Palmera De La Rosa, Ramiro David; Pertuz Cantillo, Dairo José
summary: Introducción: la familia constituye un sistema esencial para promover la salud y prevenir riesgos psicosociales. Integrar la funcionalidad familiar, la cohesión, la adaptabilidad y las redes de apoyo permite identificar factores de riesgo y de resiliencia. Objetivo: evaluar la salud familiar desde un enfoque multidimensional en familias de Santa Marta, Colombia. Método: se implementó un estudio transversal en el que se aplicaron el APGAR Familiar, el FACES III y el ecomapa digital para evaluar la funcionalidad, la cohesión-adaptabilidad y el soporte social, respectivamente. Se construyó un perfil integrado de riesgo y se estimaron razones de oportunidad (OR) mediante regresión logística binaria. Resultados: participaron 288 familias; el 59,03% presentó buena funcionalidad y el 15,21% presentó disfuncionalidad moderada o severa. Predominaron la adaptabilidad caótica (40,28%) y la cohesión relacionada (31,60%). El 70,83% presentó redes resilientes. El perfil integrado clasificó al 80,90% como moderado, al 16,67% como resiliente y al 2,43% como en riesgo. No se observaron asociaciones estadísticamente significativas entre la cohesión, la adaptabilidad o las redes de apoyo y la disfuncionalidad moderada/severa. Conclusiones: la integración de los tres instrumentos proporciona una evaluación multidimensional de la salud familiar y puede orientar la identificación de necesidades y acciones comunitarias.

title: Tendencia de resistencia bacteriana en el Magdalena, 2023–2024: hallazgos de un estudio transversal
authors: Barbosa García, Adriana R; Sánchez González, Hugo L.; Manco Cantillo, Julieth; Liscano, Yamil; Blanco Muñoz, Osmany; Aragón Muriel, Alberto
summary: Introduction: antimicrobial resistance is a public health threat, and crude rates do not describe the co-occurrence of resistance within each isolate. Objective: to characterize multidrug-resistance (MDR), co-resistance, and associated factors in bacterial isolates from a high-complexity hospital in the Colombian Caribbean. Method: a cross-sectional study was conducted using clinical isolates (2023–2024). MDR was defined according to Magiorakos; co-resistance was assessed using the φ coefficient, and associated factors were identified using log-binomial regression. Results: 1,590 isolates were analyzed. Escherichia coli (n = 650; 40.90%), Klebsiella pneumoniae (n = 282; 17.70%), Pseudomonas aeruginosa (n = 150; 9.40%), and Staphylococcus aureus (n = 137; 8.60%) were the most frequent microorganisms. Overall MDR prevalence was 32.80% and reached 67.80% in Staphylococcus epidermidis. Broad-spectrum cephalosporins showed near-perfect co-resistance (φ ≈ 1.00) and were associated with ciprofloxacin resistance (φ ≈ 0.58). After adjustment for species, ICU was not associated with MDR (adjusted prevalence ratio = 1.10; 95% confidence interval 0.94–1.28). Conclusions: MDR was mainly driven by bacterial species and co-resistance patterns; isolate-level surveillance can inform Antimicrobial Stewardship Programs (ASPs).

title: Funcionalidad familiar, diagnósticos NANDA-I y promoción de la salud mental en una comunidad vulnerable
authors: Acosta Salazar, Diana Patricia; González Noguera, Tatiana; De La Cruz Pabón, Sheris; Lapeira Panneflex, Patricia
summary: Introduction: Family functioning determines community mental health. Objective: To analyze family functioning and NANDA-I nursing diagnoses among adults in a vulnerable community of Santa Marta, and to implement a mental health promotion strategy in families with children in early childhood. Method: Mixed-methods study with a sequential design. In phase I, a cross-sectional study, 44 adults completed the Family APGAR, and researchers classified their nursing diagnoses according to the NANDA-I taxonomy. In phase II, a participatory action-research phase, 25 families with children aged 0 to 6 years received an intervention based on Nola Pender’s health promotion model. Results: 23 adults (52.27%) showed some degree of family dysfunction. The most altered domain was coping/stress tolerance, in 24 (54.55%), followed by self-perception, in 8 (18.18%). The 25 families improved family functioning, reduced punitive parenting practices, and increased early stimulation. Conclusions: Changes in coping and self-perception reflect adults' psychosocial vulnerability, and favorable changes in families with children accompanied the strategy based on Pender’s model.

authors: González Noguera, Tatiana Cecilia; Ramos de la Cruz, Ediltrudis; Acosta Salazar, Diana
summary: Schizophrenia alters the perception of reality and impairs social relationships, which hinders treatment adherence in acute care units. title: Ruina y despojo en la experiencia migratoria de la Venezuela poschavista
summary: The article analyzes the affects and emotions that emerge from the migratory experiences of Venezuelan people in Mexico since 2015, attending to their histo-ricity and effects as a “structure of feeling.” It draws on qualitative research based on semi-structured interviews and adopts a biographical approach grounded in an inductive and situated perspective, prioritizing subjective and emotion-al dimensions. The main findings identify emotions such as frustration, guilt, fear, and nostalgia, associated with ruin in a double sense: as individual down-ward mobility and as a societal process that produces a shared emotional ex-perience. Ruin is lived as a wound that enables the rearticulation, in different terms, of an ideal of the nation founded on rentier modernity, which is neverthe-less recognized as its cause. Finally, the article explores the political implications of this affective register and its derivation in a growing liberal and anti-statist sensibility.

title: Educación sexual y salud sexual en adolescentes: una revisión narrativa de la evidencia científica
authors: Cortina Navarro, Carolina Elena; Brito Jiménez, Ivone Tatiana; Oviedo, Haidy
summary: Adolescence is a crucial stage for the development of sexual health, in which comprehensive sexuality education plays a fundamental role in promoting healthy knowledge, attitudes, and practices. The objective of this narrative review was to analyze the scientific evidence on the relationship between sexuality education and sexual health in adolescents and to consider its influence on knowledge, attitudes, sexual practices, and major health outcomes. A narrative review of the scientific literature published in indexed journals and in documents from international organizations was conducted. The evidence shows that comprehensive sexuality education programs improve knowledge about sexuality, strengthen decision-making skills, promote relationships based on respect and equality, and encourage safer sexual behaviors without early initiation of sexual activity. However, their effectiveness depends on factors such as teacher training, family involvement, the sociocultural adaptation of interventions, and the support of public policies. It is concluded that comprehensive sexuality education is an effective strategy for promoting sexual health in adolescence; its strengthening requires inclusive, sustainable, and evidence-based interventions.

title: STRUCTURAL AND FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS OF EMPIRICAL RESULTS IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF DIGITAL SKILLS OF FUTURE VOCATIONAL EDUCATION TEACHERS
summary: <jats:p>The chapter presents a structural-functional interpretation of the empirical results obtained in the study of digital skills development among future vocational education teachers. The research is based on the premise that the achieved level of digital skills cannot be adequately explained by isolated quantitative indicators. The empirical results are therefore interpreted through the relationships between structural components, diagnostic criteria, empirical indicators, and their professional-pedagogical functions. The study analyzes the baseline configuration of digital skills identified at the ascertaining stage and the subsequent changes produced by the formative pedagogical intervention. Particular attention is paid to the differentiation between quantitative growth, structural reconfiguration, and functional transformation of digital skills. The findings demonstrate that the effectiveness of pedagogical influence is reflected not only in the increase of individual indicators but also in the harmonization of the internal structure of digital skills and the expansion of students’ capacity for professionally meaningful digital action. The integrated interpretation confirms the interdependence between the cognitive-informational, operational-technological, structural-integrative, and motivational-reflexive dimensions of digital skills development. The results substantiate the analytical value of the proposed structural-functional approach for evaluating systemic changes in the professional preparation of future vocational education teachers.</jats:p>

title: Football Tournaments and Economic Sentiment: Cross-Country Evidence from Europe
summary: <jats:p>Do major football tournaments move economic sentiment, and does it matter whether a country's national team takes part? We combine the European Commission's harmonized business and consumer surveys for the 27 EU member states from 1991 to 2025 with 17 World Cups and European Championships. The Economic Sentiment Indicator is about 2.3 points higher in tournament months than in other months of the same calendar year, but it is similarly elevated in the two months before; consumer confidence shows no robust pattern. Because the tournament calendar is common to all countries and almost all tournaments fall in even years, this association rests on 17 events and cannot be separated from a broader two-year rhythm in sentiment; relative to randomly drawn years, it is unusual before 2020 and marginal in the full sample (p = 0.08 to 0.14). Participation varies across countries and can be tested with full time fixed effects, under weaker assumptions. We find no statistically significant participation premium in the baseline specification and no participation-specific jump at kick-off in any specification; large premia are hard to reconcile with the data, smaller ones remain possible.</jats:p>

title: The Role of Employment and Redistribution for Lifetime Income Inequality in Denmark
authors: Jonas Maibom; Trine Schack; Rune Vejlin
summary: <jats:p>Using Danish administrative data from 1980–2023, we analyze lifetime income (both earnings and net-income) inequality and its evolution across cohorts. Earnings inequality rises with age from midlife onward and is highest among the low educated and lowest among those with medium education. Differences in employment attachment — such as non-employment and part-time work — account for 30–60 percent of lifetime earnings dispersion, and are particularly important among the low educated. Weak employment attachment is a key driver of lifetime earnings inequality and is closely linked to exposure to adverse shocks such as unemployment and health-related events. Lifetime earnings inequality has risen across cohorts among the low educated, partly through growing dispersion in employment attachment. In moving from earnings to net-income, transfers account for roughly five times as much of the inequality reduction as taxes, but this equalizing effect has weakened over time. Our results highlight the role of employment dynamics and social insurance for lifetime inequality.</jats:p>

title: Rigged from Birth: How inequality steals futures in Asia and the five public services that can reverse it
authors: Arimbi Wahono; Sabrina Salameh; Sze Vei Leong; Mustafa Talpur; Myrah Nerine Butt
summary: <jats:p>Asia's inequality crisis is also a public services crisis. Across 19 Asian economies, the poorest half of the population earns less than the richest 1%. Decades of 'growth at any cost', privatization and austerity have starved public services, leaving access to care, social protection, health, education and digital services decided by ability to pay. Yet inequality is a political choice. This paper shows how universal, high-quality public services, financed through progressive taxation, can break the vicious cycle of inequality. It calls on Asian governments to make public provision the default and fund it fairly.</jats:p>

title: Income, Wealth, and Redistribution in a Tax Haven: Distributional National Accounts for Switzerland
authors: Enea Baselgia; Remo Gurtner; Julian Koller; Isabel Z. Martínez
summary: <jats:p>This paper analyzes the composition and distribution of national income, private wealth, and the extent of redistribution in Switzerland from 2003 to 2022, combining micro tax, survey, and national accounts data. Constructing Distributional National Accounts (DINA) requires addressing two features of the Swiss setting. Switzerland is a tax haven, so we correct for cross-border profit shifting by multinationals. It is also fiscally decentralized. Lacking nationally representative tax microdata, we reweight cantonal micro tax records to match national distributions. We find that pre-tax income inequality is substantially higher than suggested by tax statistics: the top 1% income share increases by 50% once retained earnings and privileged dividends are included. Compared to previous estimates, wealth inequality is somewhat higher but shows no upward trend. The overall Swiss tax-and-transfer system is close to flat across most of the distribution, at around 45% of pre-tax income, declining to below 30% for the top 0.01%.</jats:p>

authors: Trigo Martínez, Eduardo; Garayeta Bajo, Asier; Corral Lage, Javier; Peña Esteban, Joseba Iñaki de la
summary: Purpose – This study examines the relationship between corporate governance and asset risk estimation models at the aggregate and sector-specific levels.Theoretical framework – The European Union promotes best practices in corporate governance, and as a result Spain requires compliance with the Corporate Governance Report and Recommendations.Design/methodology/approach – Using accounting information and mandatory public disclosures, the study estimates multiple linear regression models to examine the relationship between the main dimensions of corporate governance (remuneration, monitoring and governance structure) and asset risk.Findings – At the cross-sectoral level, the analysis shows that most of the variability in asset risk depends on two control variables (size and membership of the financial sector) and one variable related to corporate governance (the percentage of proprietary directors). The results do not provide statistically significant evidence to support the hypotheses concerning the variables related to corporate governance, which justifies the need for a sectoral analysis. Once intersectoral heterogeneity is eliminated, the presence of blockholders, executive remuneration, the existence of proprietary directors, and the number of board meetings explain a significant proportion of the intrasectoral variability.Practical & social implications of research – Regulators can promote governance structures; investors can assess their risk profile based on the size and sector of the firm; and boards of directors can adapt corporate governance to their sector.Originality/value – The study uses mandatory public information available since 2018 to examine the link between corporate governance and asset risk, highlighting cross-sectoral heterogeneity and the need for sectoral analysis.

title: The effect of electronic word of mouth: how credibility shapes consumer purchase intentio
summary: Purpose – This study aims to explore the impact of electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) credibility on purchase intention, with eWOM adoption and product attitude acting as mediators.Theoretical framework – The research links eWOM credibility to consumer purchase intention, using the cognition-affection-behaviour (CAB) model. A structural equation model (SEM) was constructed using SmartPLS 4.0.Findings – The findings indicate that eWOM credibility is influenced by the homophily of the source, strength of the argument and trustworthiness of the source, which ultimately affect purchase intention. On a social level, by raising awareness of the factors that contribute to eWOM credibility, the study encourages broader conversations around transparency, digital ethics, and consumer empowerment in the online marketplace.Originality/value – To the best of the author’s knowledge, this is the first study to examine the interaction between eWOM credibility and its determinants (source homophily, argument strength, and source trustworthiness), as well as eWOM adoption and product attitude, within the CAB model framework

title: The moderating role of macroeconomic factors in the relationship between asset structure and firm value: a case study of the Nairobi Securities Exchange in Kenya — ES: El papel moderador de los factores macroeconómicos en la relación entre la estructura de activos y el valor firme: un estudio de caso del Nairobi Securities Exchange en Kenya
authors: Nkonge Habakkuk, Barine; Nduati Kariuki, Samuel; Wangombe Kariuki, Peter
summary: Purpose – The study aims to explore how macroeconomic variables moderate the relationship between asset structure and firm value among firms listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE) in Kenya.Theoretical framework – The study contributes to the existing knowledge on asset structure and firm value by introducing macroeconomic factors as moderators of firm valuation models.Design/methodology/approach – A causal-comparative research design was employed, and secondary data were collected from 51 firms listed on the NSE between 2010 and 2019. The hypotheses of the study were tested using panel data regression and multiple linear regression methods. The normality, heteroscedasticity, multicollinearity and linearity of the results were tested to verify their robustness.Findings – Asset structure significantly impacts firm value. Moreover, macroeconomic factors play a significant role in moderating the relationship between asset structure and firm value. This indicates that changes in the macroeconomic environment impact the relationship between asset structure and firm value.Practical & social implications of research – The results can be used by investors, managers and policymakers because they highlight the importance of considering macroeconomic conditions when making decisions about asset allocation, investment strategies and financial policy in emerging markets.Originality/value – The research contributes to the existing body of knowledge on emerging markets by depicting how macroeconomic variables soften the interrelation between asset structure and firm value. It provides a reputable empirical basis for future studies on firm-level financial choices in varying macroeconomic settings

summary_es: Propósito – El estudio pretende explorar cómo las variables macroeconómicas moderan la relación entre la estructura de activos y el valor firme entre las empresas enumeradas en el Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE) en Kenya. title: La conciencia en la ciencia contemporánea: conceptos, marcos y el papel estructurante de la espiritualidad
summary: The study of consciousness has become an interdisciplinary field integrating psychology, neuroscience, and philosophy of mind. This article provides a conceptual introduction by reviewing definitions, key distinctions, theories, research methods, and major open debates. It examines the ontological frameworks of dualism and monism, contemporary models of consciousness, and experimental strategies focused on neural correlates. It also builds a bridge to the psychology of meaning and spirituality, understood as a meaning-making system capable of organizing certain subjective experiences. The article concludes that consciousness research requires conceptual precision and methodological pluralism, and that spirituality can be investigated as a psychological dimension without reducing it to a metaphysical claim.

title: Strategic characterization of the cape gooseberry supply chain
authors: García Cáceres, Rafael Guillermo; Plazas Martínez, Lady Viviana
summary: This study deals with the strategic characterization of the supply chain of cape gooseberry in Colombia, an exotic fruit with high economic potential in both domestic and international markets. Using a methodology proven in other agro-industrial chains, it studies the market and identifies and analyzes the actors, links and functionalities of the chain, providing a detailed diagnosis that facilitates decision-making for the stakeholders involved. The study highlights the importance of the cape gooseberry for its nutritional and therapeutic properties and its ability to generate value through agro-industrial processing. Significant challenges are identified, such as the fragmentation of the production chain, the lack of coordination among actors and the need to standardize logistical processes, which limit competitiveness and long-term sustainability. Finally, strategies are proposed to strengthen the integration of the chain, improve logistics and capitalize on growth opportunities in international markets.

summary: Purpose – To analyze the business scenario of technology companies in the state of Paraíba, Brazil, within the scope of transient competitive advantages.Theoretical framework – The study is based on the theory of transient competitive advantage, which proposes a paradigm shift in strategy. title: A espiritualidade como recurso salutogênico: o papel do coping positivo na mitigação de estressores por discriminação religiosa
summary: Religious intolerance is a psychosocial stressor that affects central dimensions of identity and maycause psychological distress. This literature-based article analyzes positive religious and spiritual coping as a mechanism for confronting and reframing such experiences. Drawing on Pargament’s theory, it examines how benevolent reappraisal, community support, and a collaborative relationship with the sacred may moderate the association between discrimination and mental health. Sabbath observance and the use of religious garments are presented as examples of situations that may trigger prejudice and institutional conflict. The study emphasizes spirituality as a salutogenic resource and as a dimension related to human rights. It concludes that cultural and spiritual competence is relevant in clinical practice to prevent iatrogenic interventions and strengthen the resilience of affected individuals.

title: La perspectiva del conocimiento científico con respecto a la formación profesional
summary: El propósito de este estudio es conocer la perspectiva del conocimiento científico que presentan las investigaciones en torno a la temática formación profesional docente en la educación superior realizados en América Latina y México. Por otro lado, se muestran aspectos técnicos de la labor docente como: vinculación teórica-práctica, creatividad innovadora, el empleo de una metodología en el proceso de enseñanza-aprendizaje y uso de las TICS. Los resultados develaron que una de las aportaciones principales que nutren el perfil docente es la formación profesional, la cual representa una de las capacidades necesarias en la labor docente y a su vez fortalecedora del proceso de enseñanza-aprendizaje. Otros resultados subrayan la relevancia del desarrollo e implementación de estrategias didácticas intencionales en las aulas, representando las habilidades principales para la profesionalización y la calidad educativa.

title: Under Pressure: Regional Divergence and Monetary Accommodation in Canada
summary: <jats:p>This paper examines whether regional economic divergence helps explain monetary policy deviations from standard aggregate prescriptions. Using monthly Canadian data from 1999 to 2024, we estimate benchmark Taylor-type rules for the Bank of Canada and interpret the residual component, with reversed sign, as a measure of monetary accommodation relative to fundamentals. We then relate this measure to provincial labor-market conditions constructed from unemployment gaps. The main result is that greater cross-province dispersion in unemployment gaps predicts more accommodative policy relative to the benchmark rule. This relationship is robust across alternative specifications and does not appear to reflect only lower-tail distress or one-region-specific conditions. The evidence instead points to a broader regional-divergence channel, with particularly strong contrasts between fossil-industry and non-fossil provinces. Additional institutional and textual evidence suggests that regional information flows, rather than regional favoritism, may help account for this pattern. Overall, the findings suggest that regional divergence matters for monetary policy even in a central bank with a national mandate and no formal regional representation.</jats:p>

title: Economic outlook: A medium-term review of the Irish health and social care system
summary: <jats:p>Ireland’s growing and ageing population is projected to significantly increase demand for a range of health and social care services in the coming years. Responding to these increasing demands, several plans and measures are in place to address the growing capacity requirements. While it is somewhat unclear how successful these measures will be in meeting the totality of future health and social care needs, there is an ongoing concern about the fiscal sustainability of the health and social care system. While Ireland’s population is relatively young, approximately one-quarter of current government expenditure was allocated to health and social care in 2025, one of the highest proportions among European countries. Even within this budget, access to some healthcare services remains curtailed, with long waits for a range of services, and the majority of the population continues to pay out of pocket for primary care services. The international literature identifies a range of potential policy options to ensure the fiscal sustainability of healthcare systems in light of changing demographic trends. These include saving for future expenditure requirements, exploring alternative financing mechanisms, reallocating or increasing public expenditure, improving efficiency and maximising population health. In this context, a number of measures are ongoing in Ireland, including saving for the future through the Future Ireland Fund and driving efficiency gains, in particular within the hospital setting. Other policy options, such as seeking alternative financing mechanisms (generally from private sources) and continuing to increase the allocation of public expenditure to healthcare, are likely to be less viable in the Irish context. Increased consideration could be given to policies which positively impact population health, both as a means of improving the quality of life of the population and reducing demand for health and social care services. In addition to its impact on the health and social care system, demographic change will also have implications for other areas of government expenditure, including pensions. Demographic changes are occurring alongside a range of other major challenges, including an uncertain geopolitical environment, digitalisation (including rapid development in artificial intelligence), climate change and decarbonisation. These challenges also bring potential opportunities for the economy and society as a whole, and specifically for the healthcare system. However, a cross-government and agency approach is required to harness all potential benefits, to ensure the fiscal sustainability of the healthcare system and the economy at large over the medium term.</jats:p>

title: Rawls on Income Inequality and Poverty
summary: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title> <jats:p>The most important function of principles of justice, Rawls argues, is to ensure that basic social institutions do not allow arbitrary factors to determine the distribution of goods. In the cases of both severe poverty and income inequality, arbitrary factors-natural and social endowments-generally determine the distribution of social goods. In order to address the influence of endowments on distribution, Rawls's theory sets out three requirements. First, a principle lexically prior to the liberty principle requires the provision of a social minimum that prevents extreme deprivation. Second, fair equality of opportunity requires the realization of real equal opportunity. Finally, the difference principle requires that—once equal opportunity is secured—remaining inequalities must be so thoroughly to everyone's advantage that even the least advantaged benefit. The requirement of equal opportunity aims to reduce significantly the influence of social endowments, while the difference principle aims primarily to reduce that influence of natural endowments.</jats:p>

summary: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title> <jats:p>When gain has to be reported and tax paid, there is a final question as to characterizing the gain as ordinary or capital. This chapter discusses the law and policy of the capital gains preference in light of Buy Borrow Die. Although this is another topic of diminished importance under the collapsed income tax, given the ability of the wealthy to avoid tax on any gains under Buy Borrow Die, the persistence of planning mechanisms such as the "carried interest" technique employed by hedge fund managers illustrates the continued attempts by the wealthy to avoid ordinary income wage taxation. title: Inclusions in the Tax Base
summary: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title> <jats:p>This chapter begins the process of explaining the doctrinal law of the US income tax by considering what does, and does not, get included in taxable income. Looking at judicial, statutory and academic definitions of “income” reveals that the income tax, which is supposed to tax all income from labor, from capital, and both combined, does not even survive the attempt at definition. Most importantly, unrealized appreciation (the Buy step), and the proceeds of debt (the Borrow step) are not included in taxable income. Nor is the imputed income or “sweat equity” that comes from being self-employed. The income tax collapses at the definitional stage.</jats:p>

title: World Bank and Education in Latin America
summary: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title> <jats:p>The interest of international organizations in education was not exclusive to the multilateral coordination system established by the United Nations. In the 1960s, one of the economic coordination bodies created by the Bretton Woods Conference, the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development, better known as the World Bank, became an increasingly relevant actor defining, implementing, and assessing education policies for the developing countries, progressively establishing well-defined fields of action and influence, and a somewhat complementary breakdown of labor with other organizations. In Latin America, the prominence of the World Bank grew stronger during the last two decades of the twentieth century. Nowadays, it is one of the main international references in regional education policymaking, setting sectorial agendas following the production and dissemination of political guidelines based on evidence and the so-called good practices to strengthen a particular view on education: training individuals suitable for the way of existing and living in contemporary capitalism. The purpose of this chapter is to trace and assess the historical path and involvement of the World Bank in regional education policymaking based on the understanding of its rationale.</jats:p>

title: The Basic Education in Latin America
summary: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title> <jats:p>This chapter examines the evolution of basic education in Latin America between 1960 and 2024 in order to identify continuities, transformations, and persistent challenges in guaranteeing the right to inclusive, equitable, and quality education. Drawing on a historical-analytical approach and an examination of documents from international organisations, specialised literature, and recent evidence on access, educational trajectories, learning outcomes, and the conditions of educational provision, the study shows that the region has made significant progress in coverage, the expansion of compulsory schooling, and the normative recognition of the right to education. However, these advances have not translated into complete school trajectories, sufficient learning outcomes, or a sustained reduction in inequalities. The analysis shows that structural gaps linked to territory, socioeconomic status, ethnic background, disability, gender, and connectivity persist, disproportionately affecting historically excluded groups. It also underlines that improving basic education does not depend solely on expanding access, but also on strengthening the quality of learning and reducing educational inequity through the proper articulation of sustained policies. It concludes that basic education in Latin America has been a partially fulfilled promise: its future consolidation will require lasting compacts, adequate financing, and pedagogical transformations guided by equity.</jats:p>

title: Decolonization in Latin American Education
summary: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title> <jats:p>This chapter introduces a discussion of the various aspects that make up the topic and the project of decolonization in Latin America. While this topic is often widely discussed in Latin America, the truth is that the project of decolonizing education remains an unfinished task both globally and in Latin America, as educational systems still maintain structures, institutions, and policies (in areas such as curriculum standards, teacher education, and the evaluation of student learning as well as of schools and universities) that perpetuate colonial patterns. Decolonization has been a subject of both political and academic interest and has given rise to a significant number of anti-imperialist, anti-colonial, and decolonial intellectual frameworks. Specifically, this chapter focuses on debates regarding the decolonization of education in the region. The chapter addresses the main positions regarding the colonial problem, the general elements that make up proposals for educational decolonization, and, briefly, some related experiences.</jats:p>

title: Nuevas rayas del escandio en el espectro de arco en el aire, entre las longitudes de onda 3200 y 2200 IA
summary: Nouvelles raies du Scandium dans le spectre d’arc, dans l'air, entre les longueurs d’onde 3200 et 2200 U. A. Le Scandium provenant de la Torveitite de Madagascar, a l'état d’oxalate impur a été transformé en oxyde. Celui-ci par digestion dans l’acetylacétone a été transformé en acetylacétonate qui a été recristallisé dans le chloroforme. Les cristaux d’acetylacétonate + 2 mol de chloroforme ont été soumis a des sublimations repetées dans le vide, en chauffant electriquement à 215°. La partie moyenne du sublimat recristallisé dans l’alcool absolu a donné un produit exempt d'oxyde, blanc très pur. Ce dennier evaporé avec l’acide azotique a été precipité par l’ammoniaque. Les spectro grammes ont été pris sur l’apparcil en quartz de Mr. Urbain, a la Sorbonne et les mesures ont été faites au moyen d’un microscope binoculaire Zeiss au Laboratoire de M. Wien à Munich. Les résultats se trouvent résumés dans les tableaux.

La descripción de la textura celular se logró con la distribución del histograma, en cada uno de los planos de color, y en los bordes se emplearon descriptores de Fourier. Se presentan los resultados de la primera fase, implementados en la clasificación e identificación de células normales. En las fases posteriores se aplicará la caracterización de cada uno de los estadios de las células clasificadas inicialmente como displásicas, para lograr discriminar las reactivas de las que realmente tienen cambios de lesión.

title: Body Mass index in children according to nutrition knowledge of their parents
summary: The present research seeks to compare the Body Mass Index (BMI) measurements in a sample of 26 subjects between 5 and 7 years old according to the nutrition knowledge of their parents. summary: .Her-2/neu expression in gastric cancer in Bucaramanga metropolitan area between 2006 and 2009ABSTRACTIntroduction: gastric cancer has become a public health problem in the world and in Colombia is one of the leading causes of mortality. The oncoprotein Her/2 neu has shown to be an independent bad prognostic factor with a variable expression ranging from 8 - 91% and has been associated with an aggressive disease and a lesser response to treatment. Aim: to determinate the frequency of Her/2 neu and its expression in gastric carcinoma, also its histopathologic correlation in patients from the Bucaramanga Metropolitan Area during 2006 to 2009. The information was collected from clinical history and parafn blocks. The immunochemistry was made with manual HERCEPTEST method. Scores 0 and 1 were interpretated as negative, score 2 as equivocal and score 3 as positive. The samples that were equivocal underwent fuorescence immunohistochemistry in situ. Results: males predominated with 243 cases, the intestinal type was the more prevalent with 230 cases, Her/2 neu expression was positive in 46 cases and there was no signifcant statistical association with histopathological subtype or gender. Conclusions: expression of Her/2 neu was positive in 11.2% of gastric carcinomas of patients from Bucaramanga Metropolitan Area, this fnding is consistent with other reports, and neither there was any statistical signifcance association with subtype and gender. title: Germicidal effect of UV light on epiphytic fungi isolated fromblueberry
authors: Latorre, B. A.; Rojas Maya, Susana; Díaz, Gonzálo A.; Chuaqui, Hernán
summary: The present study examined the inactivation effect of ultraviolet (UV) light on the conidia of Botrytis cinerea Cladosporium cladosporioides, C. herbarum and Pestalotiopsis clavispora, common pathogens of blueberry (Vaccinium corymbosum), often found as epiphytes. The fungi were grown at 20°C in acidified potato dextrose agar (APDA) in the dark; conidial suspensions (10(6) conidia mL-1) were placed the bottom of 5 cm glass Petri plates with a maximum height of 0.5 mm. Uncovered plates were immediately exposed to either UVA (λ = 361 nm), UVB (λ = 302 nm) or UVC (λ = 254 nm) at doses between 40 and 110 mJcm². The results were expressed as survival ratios Nt/N0 (the number of colonies obtained after conidia were exposed to UV irradiance/ the total number of fungal colonies in the non-irradiated controls). The fungal-dependent rate constants (k), a measure of the mortality rate, were estimated from an exponential model. The species in order of greatest to least resistance to UV light were Cladosporium cladosporioides, C. herbarum, P. clavispora and B. cinerea. The type of fungal species and the dose of UV irradiance had a significant (P<0.001) influence on Nt/N0. The interaction between the fungal species and the UV irradiance dose was significant (P≤0.004) only when the conidia were exposed to UVB or UVC. The resistance of Cladosporium spp. to UV radiation may explain the ubiquity of Cladosporium spp. in nature and could allow for the abundant populations of Cladosporium spp. often found on the foliage, flowers and fruits of blueberries.

title: Investing in change: Education, transitional justice and impact in the Colombian peacebuilding process
summary: lnvestment in educational initiatives as transitional or transformative mechanisms in societies trying to build peace is often limited by several assumptions. First, it is often held as that education is largely a tool of prevention, and that the impact of the initiatives cannot be measured. Second, children are considered only as the «future generation» who will inherit the society, reducíng their value to their future potential and undermining their agency in the present. Third, since introducing sensitive issues into the formal education system is politically difficult and risks reopening old wounds, it is held that educational intiatives are dependent on, and thus secondary to, a sustained reconciliation or peacebuilding process. As a result of these assumptions, education is often shelved as a long-term, developmental issue in post-conflict societies, and does not benefit from the resources brought by the «peace dividend.» This article seekst to deconstruct these assumptions, and argue that educational inítiatives in fact have an observable, measurable, transformative impact on individuals, groups and societies. lf this impact is supported and sustained by economic and political investment, education can play a central role in peacebuilding and transformative initiatives.

summary: One of the more conspicuous symptoms of the anti-impunity movement in transitional justice is a growing objection towards the use of amnesty. While international standards are slowly but surely building a legal barricade to prevent amnesty and impunity, states are searching far alternative measures capable of persuading hostile actors to demobilise. One promising solution to this is Colombia's proposal far prosecutions accompanied by alternative sentencing under the Marco Jurídíco de la Paz, which aims to demobilize the guerillas and end a 50-year conflict. But for this proposal to be a genuine alternative to amnesty rather than a política! attempt to avoid international legal obligations, it must satisfy victims' requirements for truth, justice and reparations. This paper examines the potential use of alternative sentencing as a mechanism of transitional justice within the scope of the "age of accountability".

authors: García Laborda, Jesús; Díez-Bedmar, María Belén; Martín Monje, Elena; Fernández Álvarez, Miguel
summary: The Foreign Language (FL) section of Spanish University Entrance Examination (EFL-PAU) has had few revisions over the last twenty years. The Spanish government has substituted the old EFL-PAU University Entrance Examination by a high stakes Baccalaureate Final Evaluation. However, further changes are expected in the coming years. Among the most important ones for the Foreign Language Section is a deep and necessary revision with the inclusion of new types of tasks. To try and inform the decisions made for the new Baccalaureate Final Evaluation, this article reports on the quantitative and qualitative analyses conducted thanks to a pilot oral test carried out with 772 recorded candidate performances. Three main goals were established for this research: 1) to find out the most important variables which characterize foreign language learning in secondary school in Spain; 2) to find out if there is any correlation between the oral competence of students at the end of their non-compulsory secondary education (as obtained from the pilot study) and the marks students obtain in the University Entrance Examination (which does not include the oral skill); and 3) to find out any aspects related to EFL teaching and learning which may potentially enhance oral performance. The results of this paper provide rich information on the students’ foreign language learning context, the strong correlation between the written and oral competences and the need to pay attention to three variables which foster the development of oral foreign language in secondary school classrooms

title: Factors influencing farmers’ willingness to participate in water allocation trading. A case study in southern Spain
authors: Giannoccaro, Giacomo; Castillo Quero, Manuela; Berbel Vecino, Julio
summary: This study aims to uncover the factors that influence farmers’ attitudes towards water allocation trading. In the study, we simulate two water availability scenarios, an average year and a drought year, in a contingent valuation experiment with 241 farmers. A survey was held in the spring of 2012 in the Guadalquivir and Almanzora River Basins. First, we estimated a multinomial logit model to determine the factors that influence farmers to decide to participate in our hypothetical market. We then analysed the structural and socio-economic factors determining the monetary value of traded water using Heckman’s two-step model. Our results indicate that those farmers who are more innovative and have had agricultural training show a higher willingness to participate in water trading. Additionally, low water-supply guarantee and appropriate information about seasonal water availability increase the probability of participation. Higher willingness to pay (WTP) for water is found in horticulture and among farmers who grow citrus and other permanent crops; lower water selling value (WTA) is found in farms with extensive annual crops and traditional olive groves. However, monetary values (WTP/WTA) are strongly dependent on the current cost of irrigation water services. While findings of this research seem to support the idea of diffusion innovation theory, the existence of ethical concerns that might influence farmers’ acceptance of irrigation water markets needs further analysis.

authors: Rojas Arias, Nicolás; Blanco Zúñiga, Cesar René; Useche de Vega, Dalia Soraya
summary: Context: Dissolved oxygen (DO) transfer is an important matter for water quality. Several devices have been designed to supply the required DO in some bodies of water during their treatment and restoration. However, these entail a high energy consumption, thus requiring the optimization of use parameters. Method: This work studies the effect of the power and number of paddles used in a horizontal axis aerator. Measurements were made on anoxic water samples using three mechanical aerating devices made up of 6, 12, and 24 paddles while varying the rotation speed from the supplied voltage. Results: The highest values obtained for the transfer coefficient KLa are reported by devices with a greater number of blades. Nevertheless, the Standard Aeration Efficiency (SAE) and the Standard Oxygen Transfer Rate (SOTR) efficiency reveal that the 6-paddle wheels are more energy-efficient. Conclusions: It is shown that DO transfer does not depend solely on the impacts associated with the number of paddles, and that the maximum transfer efficiency is obtained with a lower number of paddles. These results contribute to improving the understanding of the operation of these mechanical systems in terms of DO transfer.

title: Underrepresentation of the construct in Spanish standardized foreign language exams: A computer assisted exam proposal
authors: Fernández Álvarez, Miguel; García Laborda, Jesús; Magal Royo, Teresa
summary: Standardized tests are a reality in a globalized world and, consequently, in the Spanish system. Language test developers have already claimed that the current model of assessment has little to do with real language use, as factors such as the shift from paper to computer, information search and other uses of language or multimodal communication are not being considered (García Laborda & Fernández Álvarez, 2021). This theoretical paper proposes (1) a novel construct for testing that incorporates new functionalities which have been shown able to test appropriately language performance in academic settings; and (2) the proposal and design of an online multimodal exam that adapts to the new needs for language assessment in the University Entrance Examination. It begins with an analysis of current research to show the need for a change in the construct, and concludes by proposing a model for this high-stakes exam, based on a new construct of language proficiency and multimodal interaction for computer-based exams. The paper concludes that this model can change the way we understand technology-based exams and could be applicable to most current exams.
